Article Title: In 2022, a rotten oak on a Florida property fell onto the house next door after tenants allegedly warned the owner about falling branches; a November 2026 appeals court has now revived the homeowner's
Article Text:
Tenants reportedly warned the owner about falling branches repeatedly, but no effective action was taken before disaster struck.

Legal battle sparked by falling tree

Why the first ruling was in favor of the property owner

Appeals court distinguishes between good trees and bad trees

What’s next?

A tree can give a property character, provide shade and become a defining feature of a neighborhood. But when years of decay have turned it into a potential hazard, ignoring the warning signs can have dire consequences. That question is now at the heart of a Florida property dispute after a homeowner whose residence was damaged when a neighbour's fallen oak tree landed on it has been given a second chance to pursue a negligence claim against the owner of the property.It relates to an incident in 2022 when a large, rotten oak tree growing on land owned by USMI Properties Five, LLC, fell over into the neighboring property of Richard Vaughan, causing significant damage to his house.The complaint, the Florida District Courts of Appeal ruled on November 6, 2026, alleged the tree had been in a deteriorating condition for years before the accident. Tenants at the adjoining property had repeatedly told the owner about falling branches but nothing effective was done to remedy the problem, Vaughan added.The property owner knew or should have known about the danger and had a duty to prevent the decaying tree from damaging the properties next door, Vaughan said.He also reported losses to his home-based business as well as damage to his home.The dispute then went to court where USMI sought judgment on the pleadings on the basis that it owed no legal duty to prevent a tree on its property from damaging the neighboring property.The company pointed to past decisions by Florida courts involving trees and vegetation that grow across property lines. The decisions recognized restrictions on the landowner’s liability for branches and roots from healthy trees encroaching on to neighboring land.The trial court sided with USMI and ruled in its favor that the company had no legal duty to avoid the damage. Vaughan's claim for negligence was thus dismissed. His separate negligence-per-se claim based on an alleged statutory violation had already been dismissed and was not part of the subsequent appeal.The Sixth District Court of Appeal, however, disagreed. In their ruling on Nov. 6, the Florida District Courts of Appeal overturned the judgment, finding that previous cases about healthy trees could not be used to automatically protect a property owner who is accused of knowingly allowing a dangerous, decaying tree to remain.The appellate court explained that the general principles of negligence in Florida recognize a legal duty when someone’s actions create a foreseeable risk of harm to others. So a property owner who knows he has a rotten tree that could damage neighboring homes may have a duty to take reasonable precautions.Also, the court clarified that the prior case law did not grant blanket immunity to owners of diseased or dangerous trees.The appeals court didn't decide if USMI was ultimately negligent, or what compensation Vaughan might get. Rather, it held that the allegations in his complaint were sufficient to establish a potential legal duty, and the case should not have been dismissed at the pleading stage. Also, the ruling sends the dispute back for further proceedings, giving Vaughan another chance to pursue his claim.Image Courtesy: istock
Article Summary: Richard Vaughan's home was damaged when a neighbour's fallen oak tree landed on it. Tenants at the adjoining property had repeatedly told the owner about falling branches but nothing effective was done to remedy the problem, Vaughan said. The trial court sided with USMI and ruled in its favor that the company had no legal duty to avoid the damage. Vaughan's claim for negligence was thus dismissed.

Article Title: A Canadian woman bought a sofa for $25 at a thrift shop; four years later, while retrieving her dropped phone, she discovered a rare Rolex hidden in the cushions that went on to fetch $191,000 at auct
Article Text:
Photo: JCK Online

What the watch was

How the find happened

Representative image of cleaning couch from Canva

Why Paul Newman Daytonas matter

The auction result

A reminder about thrift store finds

A Canadian woman bought a sofa for $25 at a thrift shop and never imagined it would become one of the most talked-about watch finds in recent memory. Four years later, while retrieving her dropped phone from between the cushions, she discovered a rare Rolex Paul Newman Daytona hidden inside, a watch that went on to fetch $191,000 at auction, according to Bob’s Watches and JCK. The discovery reads like a collector’s fantasy, but it happened in real life. The sofa was bought for $25, the watch was found by accident, and the final sale price was nearly 7,600 times the cost of the couch! Read more about it, as per the reports, here:The watch was a reference 6241 Rolex Paul Newman Daytona, a vintage chronograph with a distinctive Art Deco-style dial that collectors prize above almost any other Rolex variant. Bob’s Watches notes that the presence of a Paul Newman dial can multiply a vintage Daytona’s value several times over.The watch remained in exceptional condition despite spending years between the cushions of a couch. Bob’s Watches described the find as an exceptional story about an exceptional watch, and the photos that accompanied the sale confirmed the piece’s remarkable state. The reference 6241 is part of the vintage Daytona family, which includes some of the most coveted timepieces in the world.Current-production Daytona models are already hard to get, with waitlists spanning years, but vintage examples trade at a premium that can reach into the millions.The Canadian woman had owned the couch for about four years before the watch was discovered. She was retrieving her dropped phone from between the cushions when she found the watch, a detail that has made the story even more memorable.Bob’s Watches noted that the watch’s extended stay between the cushions did not damage it. The piece remained in exceptional condition, which likely contributed to its strong auction result. The discovery is a reminder that valuable objects can hide in unexpected places. A couch bought for $25 became the setting for one of the most remarkable watch finds in recent memory.The Paul Newman dial is a rare style of vintage Daytona dial featuring an Art Deco font. Initially, these dials were poorly received by the public, but today their presence in a vintage Daytona means the watch will sell for several times more than it otherwise would.In 2017, a reference 6239 Paul Newman Daytona, the very same one owned by Paul Newman himself, sold for a record-breaking $17.8 million including buyer’s premium. That sale made it the most expensive Rolex Daytona ever sold and the most expensive wristwatch ever sold at the time.The reference 6241 found in the couch is part of that same lineage. Its sale for $191,000 reflects the enduring demand for Paul Newman Daytona watches, even for examples that are not personally linked to the actor.The watch was auctioned by Bob’s Watches in June, where it fetched $191,000. JCK reported the sale as part of the retailer’s Fresh Finds series, which features small-batch online auctions of notable pieces.The result is a striking return on a $25 investment, though the couch itself was not the source of the value. The watch was the prize, and its condition, rarity and provenance all played a role in the final price.The sale also reflects the broader strength of the vintage Rolex market. Bob’s Watches notes that vintage Daytona prices start at roughly twice the cost of current-production models and can climb much higher depending on the dial and reference.Stories like this fuel the imagination of collectors and casual shoppers alike. The idea that a $25 couch could contain a $191,000 watch is the kind of thing that keeps people browsing thrift stores and estate sales.But such finds are rare. Bob’s Watches notes that while collectors often fantasize about stumbling across a vintage Rolex in a bag of watches or a thrift store display, real-life discoveries of this magnitude are uncommon.The Canadian woman’s story is a reminder that valuable objects can hide in plain sight. A couch bought for $25 became the setting for a discovery that turned a piece of furniture into a piece of watch history.
Article Summary: A Canadian woman bought a couch for $25 at a thrift shop and never imagined it would become one of the most talked-about watch finds in recent memory. Four years later, while retrieving her dropped phone from between the cushions, she discovered a rare Rolex Paul Newman Daytona hidden inside. The watch was auctioned by Bob’s Watches in June, where it fetched $191,000.

Article Title: In 2020, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West bought a two-acre plot near her family's Palm Springs homes for $6.3 million; in November 2026, she said she had bought another nearby house to extend their hidd
Article Text:
Kim Kardashian and Kanye West's Palm Springs property purchase in 2020

Kris and Kylie Jenner's homes feature hidden garden paths

Kim Kardashian spots a neighbouring Palm Springs home during a family visit

Kim Kardashian buys neighbouring Palm Springs home in 2026 to connect family properties

Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available information. The Times of India has not independently verified the property details, purchase prices or transaction circumstances mentioned. The information should not be interpreted as confirmation from Kim Kardashian, Kanye West or their representatives.

Kim Kardashian’s property interests in California’s Coachella Valley have gradually brought several members of her family closer together. What began with a multimillion-dollar land purchase alongside her then-husband Kanye West in 2020 has since developed into a cluster of neighbouring residences belonging to the Kardashian-Jenner family. Six years after acquiring the original plot, Kim made another property decision in the same neighbourhood. According to the PEOPLE, during a November 2026 episode of The Kardashians, Kim revealed that she had purchased a house located between her existing property and Kylie Jenner’s residence.According to the Realtor, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West entered the La Quinta property market in 2020, paying approximately $6.3 million for an undeveloped parcel covering two acres. The purchase placed them inside The Madison Club, an exclusive residential community in California's Coachella Valley, not far from the grounds used for the annual Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival.At the time, the couple were married and raising their four children, North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm. The land was intended to provide space for another family residence, with its location offering a combination of mountain scenery, landscaped surroundings and access to a nearby golf course.The acquisition also had a family connection. Kim's mother, Kris Jenner, and younger half-sister Kylie Jenner already had properties along the same street. Their homes made the neighbourhood a convenient location for family visits, particularly given the amount of time the Kardashian-Jenner family spent together.Reportedly, Kylie had acquired her own neighbouring parcel in 2019 for approximately $3.25 million, with plans to construct a substantial residence. Kris had purchased her La Quinta property in 2018 for around $12 million, according to the Realtor. The 11,000-square-foot house, previously owned by actor Sylvester Stallone , became another gathering place for the family.The La Quinta properties were not simply separate holiday residences. Their proximity allowed family members to spend time together without having to travel between different parts of California.Kris's home became particularly suited to hosting relatives and guests. According to the Realtor, the property includes seven bedrooms and seven bathrooms, along with an outdoor swimming pool, fireplaces and views of the surrounding mountains. Its size and layout provided room for family gatherings and visits from Kim, Khloé, Kourtney and other relatives.Kylie also established her residence nearby, adding another property to the family's growing presence in the community. Over time, the neighbouring homes developed a more unusual feature: concealed routes through the gardens that allowed family members to move between properties without using the main entrances.The family's existing arrangement took an unexpected turn during a visit to Kris's La Quinta residence featured in the November 5, 2026 episode of The Kardashians. During the visit, Kim mentioned that a house situated between her property and Kylie's residence had come onto the market. The available property presented an opportunity to bring the family's garden connections further together.She began considering whether purchasing it would improve the arrangement. The group subsequently took one of Kim's golf carts towards the neighbouring property to look at its outdoor space.Kim acknowledged that entering the garden without permission amounted to trespassing, making a light-hearted warning to viewers not to copy what they had done. The visit nevertheless gave her an opportunity to examine the available property's layout and views.After looking around, she considered whether the house offered a better arrangement than the property she already owned. The possibility of changing homes, rather than simply adding another residence to the family's collection, became part of the discussion.Kim eventually contacted the property's real estate agent to discuss the possibility of buying it. Her comments during the episode suggested that the financial arrangement could make a switch between the two properties workable. She explained that the agent had offered her the same price and considered selling one property for approximately half the amount involved in the transaction. The location and improved view were also factors in her decision.The conversation took place while the group was still at Kris's home. Khloé later confirmed the outcome during an interview segment in the episode, revealing that her sister had actually bought the house. The announcement established that the property visit had led to a completed decision rather than remaining an informal discussion. For Kim, the acquisition offered a way to reconsider her position within the neighbourhood while bringing her closer to Kylie.
Article Summary: Kim Kardashian and Kanye West bought a two-acre plot of land in 2020 for $6.3 million. Kris Jenner and Kylie Jenner already had properties along the same street. Their homes made the neighbourhood a convenient location for family visits. Six years later, Kim made another property decision in the same neighbourhood. She purchased a house located between her existing property and Jenner's.

Article Title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donated $26 million to 20 charities in 2026; their gifts supported food banks, children's hospitals and education programmes across the US
Article Text:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's $26 million donations reach 20 US charities

Food banks receive support to expand hunger-relief efforts

Children's hospitals and cancer care programmes among beneficiaries

Donations support children's literacy and music education

Animal welfare and community organisations also receive contributions

Swift and Kelce have supported charitable causes before

Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donated a combined $26 million to 20 charitable organisations across the United States in 2026, supporting causes ranging from hunger relief and children's healthcare to education, music programmes and animal welfare. The contributions benefited organisations in several parts of the country, including New York, Rhode Island, Kansas City, Nashville and Pennsylvania. Several recipients publicly acknowledged the donations and disclosed individual contributions, including $1 million each for Food Bank For New York City and Rhode Island Community Food Bank. The announcement also highlighted the couple's support for children's hospitals, literacy initiatives and community-based programmes, extending their philanthropic efforts across multiple sectors.According to an announcement from Swift's representative, the $26 million was distributed among 20 local and national charitable organisations. Nine of the beneficiaries are based in New York, while others serve communities in places connected to the couple, including Kansas City, Nashville, Rhode Island and Pennsylvania.The beneficiaries include City Harvest, Food Bank For New York City, New York Cares, Los Angeles Regional Food Bank, Harvesters – The Community Food Network, The Store in Nashville, Helping Harvest in Reading, Rhode Island Community Food Bank and Feeding America.Other recipients include the American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (ASPCA), Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, GRAMMY in the Schools, Education Through Music, Musical Mentors, Answer the Call and After-School All-Stars, which has programmes in New York and Cleveland.The contributions also reached three children's healthcare programmes: MSK Kids at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Hassenfeld Children's Hospital at NYU Langone and Children's Mercy Hospital in Kansas City. The donations cover food assistance, animal welfare, literacy, music education, youth development, emergency responder families and paediatric healthcare.Several food banks publicly acknowledged receiving contributions from the couple, with some revealing the amounts and explaining how the money would support their operations.Food Bank For New York City confirmed receiving $1 million from Swift and Kelce on July 2, 2026. The organisation said the contribution could help provide up to 3 million meals to New Yorkers experiencing food insecurity. It works with a network of nearly 800 soup kitchens and food pantries across the city's five boroughs, providing groceries, fresh produce and nutrition assistance.The Rhode Island Community Food Bank also announced a $1 million donation. Its chief executive, Melissa Cherney, said the contribution would help the organisation purchase and distribute nutritious, culturally appropriate food to families across the state. The food bank supports 137 member agencies working to address hunger in local communities.In its announcement, the organisation highlighted the timing of the contribution, explaining that summer is typically a slower period for food donations, increasing the need for funds to purchase food and keep pantry shelves stocked.City Harvest, another New York-based hunger-relief organisation, confirmed receiving $1 million. Its chief executive, Jilly Stephens, said the contribution would help provide food to New Yorkers at a time when visits to soup kitchens and food pantries were nearing record levels.The couple also directed contributions towards organisations providing specialised medical care to children.MSK Kids, the paediatric programme at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, was among the recipients. The contribution supports clinical care and translational research focused on improving outcomes for children and young people with cancer.Hassenfeld Children's Hospital at NYU Langone also received support. The hospital provides specialised healthcare services for infants, children and adolescents, covering a range of medical conditions.Children's Mercy Hospital in Kansas City was another beneficiary. The paediatric medical centre provides specialised treatment and healthcare services for children and their families. Its inclusion also reflects Kelce's connection to Kansas City, where he plays for the Chiefs.Educational initiatives and programmes that improve access to learning opportunities also featured prominently among the beneficiaries.Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, which provides free books to young children through a network of local partners, was among the organisations selected. Parton publicly thanked Swift and Kelce after the contribution was announced, revealing that her programme had received $2 million from the couple.GRAMMY in the Schools, an initiative supporting music education, also received funding. Education Through Music, which works with schools to provide music instruction to children, and Musical Mentors, which connects students with music educators and professional musicians, were among the other beneficiaries.After-School All-Stars, which operates programmes in New York and Cleveland, was also included. Its initiatives provide children with academic support, enrichment activities and opportunities to develop skills outside regular school hours.The American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (ASPCA) was the animal welfare organisation included in the donation list. The nonprofit works on animal rescue, veterinary care, adoption services and efforts to prevent cruelty towards animals.New York Cares, which connects volunteers with community projects and nonprofit organisations, was another recipient. Answer the Call supports families of New York City police officers, firefighters and emergency medical workers who die in the line of duty.The Store, a Nashville-based nonprofit founded by musician Brad Paisley and actor Kimberly Williams-Paisley, also benefited. It provides groceries to families experiencing food insecurity, allowing eligible individuals to access essential food supplies without cost.The contributions follow earlier philanthropic activities by both celebrities.Swift has previously donated to food banks in cities visited during her Eras Tour. Several organisations publicly acknowledged her contributions as the tour travelled across the United States. She has also supported disaster relief, children's hospitals, education initiatives and animal welfare organisations.Kelce established the Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation to support disadvantaged young people by expanding access to opportunities in education, athletics, business, science, technology, engineering, mathematics and the arts.His foundation has supported youth development initiatives, including programmes in Kansas City and Cleveland. His charitable activities have also included community outreach and initiatives aimed at helping children develop skills and access educational resources.
Article Summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donated a combined $26 million to 20 charitable organisations across the United States in 2026. The contributions benefited organisations in several parts of the country, including New York, Rhode Island, Kansas City, Nashville and Pennsylvania. Donations cover food assistance, animal welfare, literacy, music education, youth development and paediatric healthcare.

Article Title: Israel politics: Eisenkot likely to lead change bloc in Knesset, meets Lieberman today
Article Text:
Gadi Eisenkot is positioned as the top candidate to spearhead the change bloc in Israel's Knesset. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot is emerging as the frontrunner to lead the change bloc in Israel's Knesset when the legislature convenes on Tuesday.According to Israeli news outlet N12, Eisenkot is scheduled to hold talks with Yisrael Beiteinu leader Avigdor Lieberman on Monday to discuss the parliamentary leadership position. Eisenkot is currently considered the leading contender for the role.The proposed meeting comes amid ongoing political consultations following president Isaac Herzog's decision to entrust Eisenkot with the task of forming Israel's next government. The two leaders are expected to discuss, who should head the Change Bloc in the Knesset, according to news agency ANI.Eisenkot officially received the mandate on Sunday after securing recommendations from 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset during consultations with various political factions. Those backing him included lawmakers from Yashar, Together, The Democrats, Yisrael Beiteinu and Arab-led parties.After receiving the mandate, Eisenkot called for a new political chapter centred on 'Zionism, solidarity, and friendship'. He also pledged to form a broad-based national emergency government capable of addressing Israel's security, diplomatic and domestic challenges.In a post on X, Eisenkot said, 'Israel needs a new government.Israel needs leadership that champions what unites us and paves the way for a new era—an era of Zionism, solidarity, and friendship.'Describing the situation as a 'challenging and fateful state of emergency', he cited ongoing conflicts, military objectives that remain unfulfilled and what he termed a 'devastating diplomatic crisis'.While handing over the mandate, president Herzog said Eisenkot had secured the 'clear and unequivocal support' of a majority of Knesset members and was the candidate with the strongest prospects of forming the next government.However, disagreements have surfaced between Eisenkot and Lieberman over the proposed government's composition, particularly the possibility of depending on Arab-led parties for parliamentary support.Lieberman has categorically opposed backing a minority government that relies on Arab-led parties, a position that could create further hurdles for Eisenkot as he attempts to build a governing coalition.Eisenkot has 28 days to form the government. President Herzog can grant him an additional extension of up to 14 days if necessary. The meeting with Lieberman is expected to take place a day before the new Knesset is sworn in on Tuesday.
Article Summary: Gadi Eisenkot is expected to hold talks with Yisrael Beiteinu leader Avigdor Lieberman on Monday. The two leaders are expected to discuss who should head the Change Bloc in the Knesset. The proposed meeting comes amid ongoing political consultations following president Isaac Herzog's decision to entrust him with the task of forming Israel's next government.

Article Title: Iran’s hidden oil network in China: Leaked letter details Tehran’s strategy to bypass US sanctions
Article Text:
Iran expands oil operations in China despite US sanctions, confidential letter shows

How Iran and China keep oil trade flowing

China seeks deeper discounts as Iran faces pressure

Iran has secured control of oil terminals and storage facilities at several locations in China to help transport and sell its sanctioned crude despite US restrictions, according to a confidential letter obtained by Iran International and accounts from sources in Iran's Oil Ministry.The arrangement involves Iranian-controlled port facilities, long-term leases and oil storage tanks that allow sanctioned tankers to unload crude directly in China, reducing the need to transfer cargoes between vessels or rely on conventional shipping routes.In a confidential letter written by Hamid Bovard, former head of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) and current acting oil minister, in response to correspondence from Ali Shamkhani, a former secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and political adviser to then-supreme leader Ali Khamenei.In his letter, Bovard criticised the oil-trading policies of former president Ebrahim Raisi and described an alternative arrangement developed under President Masoud Pezeshkian, involving what he characterised as covert cooperation from China.According to Bovard, Iranian authorities instructed trusted oil intermediaries to continue using sanctioned vessels capable of docking at designated Chinese ports.The Iranian foreign ministry negotiated access to port facilities and oil terminals, while Tehran secured long-term leases on storage infrastructure to facilitate the direct sale of Iranian crude in the Chinese market.Two Iranian oil ministry sources told Iran International that Tehran had acquired control of facilities at three locations in China. These include a terminal in the Ningbo-Zhoushan free trade zone, where Iran reportedly gained control after helping build smaller transit facilities, as well as stakes in smaller docks at Qingdao and Pant in Shandong province.The docks are located close to pipelines, allowing crude to be transported to Chinese refineries without being transferred to other vessels, the sources said.Iran has also purchased seven oil storage tanks in China, according to the report. Four are located at the ports of Dalian and Huizhou and in the coastal cities of Dongying and Weifang. The oil ministry controls three others in the Zhoushan area of the Ningbo-Zhoushan archipelago, including facilities on Aoshan and Shulanghu islands and in the Zengyamuo oil zone.The facilities are reportedly being used by tankers linked to Hossein Shamkhani, son of Ali Shamkhani, who operates a shadow fleet. Iran International said the arrangement allows these vessels to continue delivering Iranian crude despite US sanctions. The US Treasury has sanctioned 51 vessels linked to Hossein Shamkhani.China has long been central to Iran's efforts to sustain oil exports despite US sanctions. It is the biggest buyer of Iranian crude, with independent Chinese refineries, commonly known as “teapot” refineries, purchasing much of the oil through intermediaries.China accounted for more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil exports in 2025, averaging around 1.4 million barrels per day, according to Kpler data cited in a Reuters report.The two countries have also developed a barter-like payment mechanism that allows Iran to convert oil proceeds into credits for purchasing Chinese goods, bypassing conventional international banking channels.Under the arrangement, proceeds from Iranian oil sales are channelled through a special-purpose vehicle (SPV), which pays Chinese suppliers for goods ranging from medicines and vehicles to communication equipment.The system allows Chinese companies to receive payments without directly dealing with Iranian buyers or using conventional international banking channels, limiting their exposure to US sanctions. China, meanwhile, continues to access discounted Iranian crude.Despite the arrangements, Bovard's letter suggests that Tehran has faced growing resistance from Beijing over its oil trade. According to the correspondence, China rejected Iran's request to increase crude import quotas for Chinese refineries, raised purchases from Venezuela and demanded deeper discounts on Iranian oil.The letter also exposed tensions within Iran's oil-trading network, particularly over the role of Hossein Shamkhani and other intermediaries.Bovard alleged that Hossein Shamkhani had used loans from the Iranian government to purchase vessels but deployed them to transport Russian oil rather than Iranian crude. He also accused him of receiving Iranian oil on consignment without providing collateral and selling it on the market.Bovard portrayed the United Arab Emirates as Shamkhani's exclusive trading domain, alleging that the oil ministry had effectively become an agent for his business interests.The letter also disputed Ali Shamkhani's assessment of the discounts at which Iranian oil was being sold. Shamkhani had reportedly told Khamenei that the discount stood at 50 cents per barrel under Raisi, compared with $9 per barrel under Pezeshkian.The latest disclosures follow an earlier Iran International report in September, which said that Mohammad Javad Bavand, a special assistant to the oil minister, had instructed four intermediaries, including Hossein Shamkhani, to sell 86 million barrels of Iranian crude at an 8.5% discount.Although China remains Iran's most important oil customer, the reported demand for larger discounts and restrictions on import quotas suggest that Beijing's willingness to accommodate Tehran may have limits.
Article Summary: Iran has secured control of oil terminals and storage facilities at several locations in China to help transport and sell its sanctioned crude. The arrangement involves Iranian-controlled port facilities, long-term leases and oil storage tanks that allow sanctioned tankers to unload crude directly in China. Iran International said the arrangement allows these vessels to continue delivering Iranian crude despite US sanctions.

Article Title: 'You'll know soon enough': Trump's warning on 'destroying' rest of Iran

US President Donald Trump on Thursday (local time) issued a fresh warning to Iran, saying Washington could take further action against the country while signalling that he would prefer to avoid additional destruction. Iran has reportedly sent a fresh proposal on its nuclear programme to the US through Qatar, but Tehran has said negotiations would depend on Washington meeting its demands, including lifting sanctions, releasing frozen Iranian assets and paying reparations. The US is reviewing the proposal, even as Trump has kept the option of renewed military action open. Tensions also remain high around Strait of Hormuz.

Article Title: Earthquake of magnitude 5.0 jolts China's Xinjiang region
Article Text:
China's Xinjiang hit by 5.0-magnitude earthquake, says NCS

An earthquake of magnitude 5.0 struck China's Xinjiang region at 10:26 pm IST on Thursday, the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said.According to the NCS, the earthquake was recorded at 22:26 IST.The earthquake's epicentre was located close to the international border between India and China.There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.
Article Summary: An earthquake of magnitude 5.0 struck China's Xinjiang region at 10:26 pm IST on Thursday. The earthquake's epicentre was located close to the international border between India and China. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.

Article Title: Midterm losses, no exits: Marco Rubio rules out quitting, Donald Trump backs Pete Hegseth
Article Text:
File photo - US President Donald Trump speaks during a media conference as Marco Rubio, right, and Pete Hegseth listen

Rubio backs JD Vance for 2028 presidential race

White House rejects reports of Rubio's possible exit

US secretary of state Marco Rubio has dismissed reports that he is considering leaving the Trump administration following the Republican Party's setbacks in the midterm elections, saying that completing President Donald Trump's second term has “always been my plan”.In an interview with The New York Times, Rubio rejected speculation that he might step down ahead of a possible 2028 presidential campaign and declined to discuss his political ambitions.“Working for President Trump until the end of his term has always been my plan,” Rubio said, adding that he did not know where reports about his possible departure had originated.“I love the work I’m doing,” he said. “And plus I always laugh when they say he’s going to leave his job. I go, ‘Which one?’”Rubio, who also serves as Trump's national security adviser, refused to entertain questions about whether he was considering a presidential run in 2028.“I literally will not talk about 2028 anymore,” he told the newspaper in his White House office. “I just won’t do it.”Rubio has previously indicated that he would support Vice President JD Vance if he decided to run for president in 2028.“JD is a very good friend of mine,” Rubio told NBC News in May. “If JD runs for president, I think he’d be a phenomenal candidate. I’ve said publicly, and I’ll say it again, I’ll be the first person to sign up and support him.”However, Vance's post-election assessment on Wednesday included criticism of the administration's approach to the Iran war, its policy on Israel and its messaging on the economy.The vice-president blamed the war with Iran for the Republicans' election setbacks and said voters had turned against the administration's position on Israel and its handling of economic concerns. Trump has closely aligned himself with Israel and dismissed concerns over affordability as a “hoax”.Asked whether he agreed with Vance's assessment, Rubio initially deflected, saying he was not “really involved in domestic politics”.However, Rubio acknowledged the political implications of the Iran war when he appeared alongside Trump at a rally in Kansas on Sunday. Trump praised the secretary of state and joked that he might have to fire him because he had become “too popular”.Explaining his presence at the rally, Rubio said he was travelling with the president as the designated national security official. He also acknowledged Trump's remarks that the war had been a factor in the election results.“Higher prices at the gas pump, I acknowledge, is not like the kind of thing you campaign on and brag about,” Rubio said.However, he defended Trump's decision to take action despite its potential political costs, saying the president “deserves a tremendous amount of credit” for doing what he considered necessary.“Ultimately, that is the price of leadership — is the willingness to do things that may not be politically popular or expedient but are necessary for your country and its long-term future,” he said.The White House and the State Department have also rejected reports that Rubio could leave his position following the Republican setbacks.White House spokesperson Beni Rae Harmony described the reports as a fabricated hoax circulated by anonymous sources, while assistant secretary of state for global public affairs Dylan Johnson called them baseless fake news.The speculation over a possible administration shake-up has also involved defence secretary Pete Hegseth , whose handling of the Iran war has drawn criticism following the election losses.The White House has denied reports that Hegseth and Rubio might leave their positions. Trump told ABC News that he had received calls about Hegseth but had “every intention” of keeping him. He later praised the defence secretary, saying he had “done a fantastic job”.However, Republican Representative Thomas Massie has said he intends to move ahead with an effort to impeach Hegseth, with a resolution expected as early as next week. Hegseth has rejected the effort, describing it as a politically motivated attempt to undermine him.Separately, The Washington Post reported that Trump could be considering replacing General Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, or Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command.Both have played significant roles in providing guidance on the Iran war.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio has dismissed reports that he is considering leaving the Trump administration following the Republican Party's setbacks in the midterm elections. In an interview with The New York Times, Rubio rejected speculation that he might step down ahead of a possible 2028 presidential campaign. The White House and the State Department have also rejected reports that Rubio could leave his position.

Article Title: Namaste Uncle Sam: Nithya Raman poised to become LA Mayor, as America's top two cities get desi touch
Article Text:
Elected LA mayor Nithya Raman and New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Nithya Raman's background

How Socialists are storming across American cities:

Indian origin winners from the US midterm elections

Nithya Raman stood before supporters at a downtown Los Angeles brewery in June, struggling to hold back tears. The early primary election returns had placed her third in the race for mayor, behind incumbent Karen Bass and reality tv personality Spencer Pratt, and it looked like the end of the road for her. She gave what was almost a concession speech. Her father Venkit Raman, an IITian, comforted campaign workers, telling them her full name Nithya Varsha means 'everlasting monsoon,' and her political life would be replenished soon.It came sooner than anyone expected because after all this is the la la land of Hollywood where plot twists are common. And appropriately too enough considering her husband, Vali Chandrasekaran, is a successful television writer and producer whose credits include 30 Rock and Modern Family. A batch of late ballots that came in took Raman past Pratt to second place, and because Bass did not get 50 per cent of the vote, there would be a run-off election in November. Even then, few gave the 45-year old political tyro, with only six years of experience on the City Council, any chance. Raman herself had once supported Bass, and the 73-year old party stalwart had the backing of the Democratic establishment, including endorsements from Kamala Harris, Nancy Pelosi and Governor Gavin Newsom.She had experience, name recognition, and the advantage of incumbency.What Bass could not quite escape was the perception that Los Angeles is broken and she did not have the toolkit to fix it. The devastating January 2025 Palisades wildfire, which killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of homes, became a defining political liability. Bass was abroad when the mishap occurred and her handling of the disaster and recovery became a persistent political liability. Raman’s campaign ignited. She offered herself as the candidate of change, promising better housing, improved public services and more accountable government. An urban planner by training, she could talk about the nuts and bolts of city administration rather than simply deliver ideological sermons. On Tuesday night, her persistence paid off, and although the race has not been officially called, she is ahead by 25,000 votes and looks likely to seal the deal. She invited supporters to join her in a dance on Wednesday, the tears in June now forgotten.Raman's victory is more than an extraordinary personal turnaround. It is another major breakthrough for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), the left-wing movement that has been steadily challenging the Democratic Party establishment. And for India, it provides an especially striking political subplot: New York and Los Angeles, America's two largest cities, will now be led by mayors of Indian origin, with Zohran Mamdani already in office in New York.What's even more striking: Long before Mamdani and Raman began making their mark in American municipal politics, several prominent Indian nationalists and intellectuals had encountered the country's radical political traditions first hand. Lala Lajpat Rai spent five years in the U.S between 1914 and 1919, establishing the India Home Rule League and publishing the journal Young India in New York. The radical humanist M.N. Roy arrived in the U.S in 1916 as a global itinerant, encountered American radicals and began studying socialism, subsequently moving to Mexico City, where he founded the Communist Party of Mexico in 1919. He later played a foundational role in establishing the Communist Party of India in 1920. B.R. Ambedkar, meanwhile, studied at Columbia University in NYC, encountering some of America's leading liberal and progressive intellectuals, including philosopher John Dewey. And Jayaprakash Narayan spent seven years in America (1922-1929), studying at Berkeley, Iowa, and Wisconsin, where he encountered Marxism and returned to India a committed socialist.All this was at a time socialism was enjoying considerable electoral popularity. In 1912, Socialist Party presidential candidate Eugene Debs won nearly a million votes, then about 6% of the national total. Socialists also held hundreds of municipal offices, including mayoralties. In fact, in the early 1950s Donald Trump’s father Fred Trump clashed with the folk singer Woody Guthrie, an avowed socialist, over racial segregation and housing discrimination in Brooklyn, causing him to write a song -- a scalding takedown of a predatory landlord -- titled “Old Man Trump" who stirred up racial hatred "in the bloodsport of the human heart. "Indeed, even in the modern era, the current upsurge of socialists did not emerge overnight. One of its earliest conspicuous faces was another Indian activist: Kshama Sawant, born in Pune and raised in Mumbai, who won a seat on Seattle's City Council in 2013. A former economics professor and member of Socialist Alternative rather than the DSA, Sawant became a prominent voice for a $15 minimum wage, rent control and taxing the wealthy. Her victory demonstrated that a politician openly identifying with socialism could win in an American city.Bernie Sanders subsequently took the argument national with his presidential campaigns in 2016 and 2020 bringing democratic socialism into mainstream political conversation, particularly among younger Americans frustrated by inequality, expensive healthcare, housing costs and the influence of corporate money. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's (AOC’s) stunning 2018 primary victory over veteran Democrat Joe Crowley gave the movement another national face. The election of Mamdani as New York mayor in 2025 was an even bigger breakthrough. Mamdani defeated Democratic political heavyweight Andrew Cuomo by campaigning on affordable housing, free bus services, universal childcare and a city government that would work for ordinary people.The movement now has a growing presence in municipal government. Besides Mamdani in New York, democratic socialist or DSA-affiliated mayors include Katie Wilson in Seattle, Janeese Lewis George in Washington DC, Emma Mulvaney-Stanak in Burlington, Robert Cantelmo in Ithaca and Eduardo Martinez in Richmond, California. In the mid-terms, six DSA-endorsed candidates have won seats in the House of Representatives: Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez in New York (both backed by Mamdani), Melat Kiros in Colorado, Angela Gonzales-Torres in California, Donavan McKinney in Michigan and Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania. DSA members Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib also won re-election.The organisation's own election tracker reported victories across an even wider range of state and local contests, including in Florida, Maryland, Washington, Oregon, Pennsylvania and Vermont. The significance is not simply the number of elected socialists, but their willingness, like in the case of Raman v Bass, to challenge Democratic incumbents and party leadership rather than wait patiently for establishment approval.While their electoral success is undeniable, the jury is still out on their ability to translate ambitious promises of affordable housing, safer streets, better transport and sustainable municipal finances into reality. Governing New York or Seattle or LA is considerably more complicated than winning an election with a catchy slogan. Already, MAGA bros are cranking up right wing fearmongering with Conservative commentators Benny Johnson invoking scenarios of urban 'Armageddon' a favorite Trump theme.For now though the socialists are having their moment in the sun. The MAGA crowd is predicting an apocalypse, the billionaires are checking their property portfolios, and the Democratic establishment is wondering whether it should start taking out membership in the DSA. Raman and Mamdani now have the rather unenviable task of proving that running a city is not quite the same as running against one. In the process, America's urban political landscape is getting a makeover — and this time, the revolution has an Indian accent.
Article Summary: Nithya Raman and Zohran Mamdani are the new mayors of Los Angeles and New York City respectively. Raman's victory is another major breakthrough for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), the left-wing movement that has been challenging the Democratic Party establishment.

Article Title: A Scottish wildlife rescuer saved a starving badger cub trapped in a cattle trough, but officials denied his request to keep her; now he is fighting to retain the animal he says cannot survive in the
Article Text:
Rescued from a cattle trough in April, Harriet was nursed back to health by ecologist Graeme Wilson.

From a desperate rescue to an unusual bond

Why the ecologist wants to keep Harriet

Wildlife experts raise concerns

Harriet's future remains uncertain

Images Courtesy: istock and BBC

A chance encounter with a helpless animal has turned into a complicated battle over wildlife protection, rehabilitation and the limits of human intervention. When Scottish ecologist Graeme Wilson rescued a starving badger cub from a cattle trough, he expected to nurse her back to health. Instead, the experience left him convinced that returning her to the wild could put her life in danger. Now, he is fighting for permission to give Harriet a permanent home, despite opposition from wildlife authorities.According to the BBC, Harriet was discovered in April trapped inside a cattle trough, around 100 metres from her sett in the Scottish Borders. Wilson was called to help the young animal and took responsibility for her recovery, gradually nursing her back to health.However, her behaviour soon raised concerns about whether she could survive independently. Given her bottle feeding response and familiarity with humans, Wilson suspected Harriet was hand-reared before her rescue.As reported by The Telegraph, Wilson believes the cub has become accustomed to humans to such an extent that releasing her into the countryside could expose her to serious risks. He fears she might approach people while out walking, potentially placing herself in a dangerous situation.Wilson operates GW Ecology, an independent wildlife rescue and rehabilitation service from his home in Denholm. Alongside caring for injured animals, his work involves ecological surveys to identify protected species at proposed development sites. He also organises bat walks, workshops and educational activities to encourage greater awareness of wildlife conservation.The ecologist applied to NatureScot for an educational licence that would allow him to continue caring for Harriet while helping the public understand badgers and the challenges involved in rehabilitating protected wildlife.However, the application was rejected. NatureScot suggested that Harriet should either be returned to the wild or transferred to a zoo. Wilson believes neither option would adequately address her circumstances. While a release could expose her to injury or death, he fears a conventional zoo environment would leave her isolated and distressed.The disagreement has brought wider questions about the responsibilities involved in wildlife rehabilitation into focus. The BBC reported that the British Wildlife Rehabilitation Council has stressed the specialist nature of caring for wild animals.Paul Reynolds, who chairs the organisation, has highlighted the importance of suitable facilities, species-specific care, veterinary supervision and an understanding of an animal's natural behaviour. The council also distinguishes responsible rehabilitation from keeping wild animals permanently in captivity for educational or personal purposes.According to The Telegraph, the organisation maintains that an animal becoming accustomed to human contact should not automatically be considered grounds for permanent captivity.NatureScot has indicated that discussions with Wilson and other relevant organisations are continuing in an effort to find a practical resolution. The authority has emphasised that Harriet's welfare remains central to its decision-making process. Police Scotland has also been made aware of the situation.Meanwhile, the Scottish SPCA advises people who encounter sick or injured badgers to contact its rescue officers rather than attempting to handle the animals themselves. Young cubs found away from their setts may need help, and frightened or injured badgers may attack.Wilson still wants a safe future for Harriet. Whether that means an exception to the usual rules or another arrangement, the case highlights the difficult balance between individual animal welfare and the principles of wildlife conservation.
Article Summary: Harriet the badger cub was rescued from a cattle trough in April. Ecologist Graeme Wilson nursed her back to health but is now fighting for permission to give her a permanent home. The British Wildlife Rehabilitation Council has stressed the specialist nature of caring for wild animals.

Article Title: Ava Marie Musci of Liverpool, New York, set up a lemonade stand at age 8 to fight childhood cancer; ten years later she has raised $22,000, enough to fund 450 hours of research, and been named one of
Article Text:
Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation supports research into childhood cancer (Photo: ALSF)

Ten years of helping cancer research

Ava's career plans shaped by fundraising

Ava Marie Musci of Liverpool, New York, was eight years old when she decided to do something to help children fighting cancer. After learning about Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation, she was inspired by the difference one young girl had made while facing serious challenges of her own. Ava therefore decided to start a lemonade stand in her neighbourhood and use the money raised to support childhood cancer research.What started as a small effort has continued for a decade now and Ava has raised $22,000 for Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation, an organisation that supports research into childhood cancer. According to This Is CNY, the money has helped fund 450 hours of cancer research.The initiative has also grown beyond a neighbourhood lemonade stand. Over the years, several local businesses and organisations have joined her efforts, helping turn the fundraiser into a community-supported activity.Ava's work has also earned her recognition among Central New York's outstanding high school students. She was among the 20 students honoured at the 2026 Best and Brightest Awards organised by Syracuse.com and The Post-Standard on November 5 at the Redhouse Arts Center in Syracuse.The awards recognise the achievements of high school seniors graduating in 2027. Students were selected based on their academic performance, extracurricular activities, leadership and contributions to their schools and communities.Ava first came across Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation when she was eight. Learning about the work of the foundation inspired her to take action. She started a lemonade stand in her neighbourhood and began collecting money for paediatric cancer research.The initiative continued over the following years. What started with Ava selling lemonade gradually attracted support from different parts of the community.Wegmans, Costco, Walmart and the Onondaga County Sheriff's Office were among the organisations that contributed supplies and support. Their involvement helped Ava continue the fundraiser and expand its reach.Over 10 years, her efforts resulted in $22,000 being raised for the foundation. The amount has funded 450 hours of cancer research.Sarah McIntosh of Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation praised Ava's efforts and her ability to bring people together.“What Ava built with her lemonade stand shows her strong leadership skills and ability to rally people together to make a difference and to push for a better future,” McIntosh said.The work also influenced how Ava looks at her future. Through her community service, she realised that an individual's efforts can make a difference.She is now pursuing her interest in criminal justice and forensics. Ava was selected for the BOCES New Visions Criminal Justice Program, where she continues to excel.After completing high school, she hopes to attend the University at Albany. She plans to study criminal justice and forensics, or digital forensics.Alongside her community work and academic interests, Ava is involved in several activities at school. She plays soccer and is a member of the girls' wrestling team. She is also part of the marching band and regularly volunteers at her church.Ava also manages several part-time jobs, including working as a youth soccer referee.Her selection for the Best and Brightest Awards recognises these achievements alongside her contribution to the community.The 2026 awards honoured 20 students from Central New York. Eligible students had to maintain at least a B grade or a 3.0 grade point average and attend schools in the region.Students submitted applications detailing their academic achievements, extracurricular activities and community service. They also provided letters of recommendation and personal narratives. A panel of Syracuse.com judges selected the winners.
Article Summary: Ava Marie Musci of Liverpool, New York, has raised $22,000 for Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation. The money has funded 450 hours of childhood cancer research. Ava's work has also earned her recognition among Central New York's outstanding high school students.

Article Title: North Dakota parents gave a son an option to buy farmland for $100 an acre if he returned and farmed; after an inheritance fight, the Supreme Court ruled he failed the condition and ordered rent damag
Article Text:
A man lost the chance to buy his parents’ farmland for $100 an acre after failing to meet their farming condition. (AI image)

Why the court rejected his claim

Sister seeks compensation for use of farmland

Court also limits brother's claim to land

A North Dakota man has lost his claim to buy his parents' farmland for $100 an acre after the state Supreme Court ruled that he failed to meet a condition set out in their wills. The parents had offered their son, Todd Stramer, the option to purchase the remaining farmland at the fixed price if he returned to North Dakota and actively farmed it. According to the ruling dated Friday, the court upheld the finding that Todd had not fulfilled this condition. It also ordered a lower court to reconsider damages for his use of the farmland between 2023 and 2025.The dispute began after William and Elaine Stramer made their wills in July 2013. The couple had five children, Todd, Ann, Douglas, Steve and Matthew. Their wills gave Todd the option to buy the remaining farmland for $100 an acre. However, he had to move back to North Dakota and actively farm the property. He also had to exercise the option within one year of the death of the surviving parent.According to the offer, if Todd completed the purchase, he would also receive the farm machinery, equipment and the balance in the checking account. William died in January 2015, and Todd moved back to North Dakota. Elaine died in November 2022. Todd then informed the estate that he wanted to exercise his purchase option.However, his siblings challenged his claim. The dispute eventually reached the North Dakota Supreme Court, which examined whether Todd had actually been farming the property as required by his parents.For the 2023 farming season, Todd arranged for Mike Appert, a longtime tenant of the family, to grow corn and soybeans on the land. Appert supplied the seeds and used his own employees and equipment to plant, spray and harvest the crops.Todd did not pay rent for the farmland. The Elaine Stramer Irrevocable Trust paid the farming expenses and reported the profits and losses in its tax filings.Todd argued that he had taken an active role in managing the farming operation. The lower court accepted that he had contributed to its management. However, it found that he had not independently provided enough money, equipment or land for the operation.The court examined the federal Farm Service Agency's definition of being actively engaged in farming. Under this definition, a person must contribute capital, equipment or land, along with personal labour or management. The person's share of profits or losses must also match their contribution, and they must face a financial risk.The Supreme Court agreed with the lower court's use of this definition. The couple's estate planning lawyer, Charles Chapman, told the trial court that William Stramer had used the expression while referring to federal farm programmes.Chapman recalled asking William what active farming meant. William replied that "anybody who knows anything about farming knows what that means".The court also considered testimony from Appert, who had been farming for more than 35 years and worked on about 47,000 acres.The records showed that the family trust paid for the farming operation. Todd did not use his own money to fund it or maintain a separate business account. Appert provided the equipment, while the trust paid for its use.The Supreme Court said Todd could have contributed by leasing the land or equipment at fair market value. However, he did not do so. His interest in the farmland through the purchase option was not enough to meet the requirement.The court therefore upheld the finding that Todd had not actively farmed the property within the required period. He could not validly exercise the option to buy it.The case also involved Todd's role in managing his mother's estate and trust. After Elaine's death, he became the personal representative of her estate and was named trustee of the Elaine Stramer Irrevocable Trust.His sister Ann sought his removal from both positions in 2023. The lower court removed him after finding that he had violated his duties. The Supreme Court upheld this decision.Ann also challenged the lower court's refusal to award compensation for Todd's use of the farmland between 2023 and 2025.She argued that he should pay $700,104 for the three years. Her calculation was based on the $233,368 rent that Appert had paid for the farmland in 2022.The Supreme Court agreed that Todd's occupation of the property was wrongful because he had failed to meet the condition for buying it. It said the estate was entitled to damages for the use of the land.However, the court said the full rent from the property could not be used to calculate the amount owed to Elaine's estate. The farmland was divided into two equal interests. One half belonged to the William Stramer Disclaimer Trust, while the other half belonged to Elaine's estate.Appert had paid $233,368 in rent for 2,333.68 acres in 2022. The amount was divided into two equal payments of $116,684, one for each trust. The Supreme Court said the rental value of Elaine's half was therefore $116,684 a year.The court said compensation could be calculated using either the fair rental value of Elaine's share or the income generated from it. However, the records did not clearly establish who received all the farming income between 2023 and 2025.It reversed the lower court's decision on damages and sent the matter back for the amount to be calculated.The Supreme Court also considered a separate claim by Todd's brother Douglas, who wanted to buy land around his house.Their parents' wills gave Douglas an option to purchase the immediate farmyard for $100 an acre. He argued that this covered 25 acres identified in a survey completed in November 2014.However, the court found that the survey had been prepared for a proposed purchase that included additional land for Douglas's beekeeping business. It was not meant to identify the farmyard covered by the will.Douglas had testified that the actual farmyard measured about 5.96 acres. The Supreme Court ruled that his purchase option covered 5.96 acres, not the entire 25 acres.The court partly upheld and partly reversed the lower court's decisions. It sent the case back for the judgment to be amended and for damages arising from Todd's use of the farmland to be calculated.
Article Summary: Todd Stramer was offered the option to buy his parents' farmland for $100 an acre if he returned to North Dakota and actively farmed it. The North Dakota Supreme Court upheld the finding that Todd had not fulfilled this condition. It also ordered a lower court to reconsider damages for his use of the farmland between 2023 and 2025. Todd argued that he had taken an active role in managing the farming operation.

Article Title: Mexico arrests an alleged cartel leader wanted in the US and 19 others after a raid using DEA intelligence, with authorities linking the suspect to a mayor's killing and extortion of avocado producers
Article Text:
Shootout during arrest operation

Why is the suspect linked to a mayor's murder?

How avocado producers became cartel targets

A wider crackdown on the cartel network

The lucrative avocado business in western Mexico has long been shadowed by threats, extortion and cartel violence. In one of the latest developments in the region's fight against organised crime, Mexican authorities have arrested an alleged drug cartel leader wanted in the United States, along with 19 other people, in an operation aided by intelligence shared by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). The main suspect, Rafael "N", known by the alias "R2", is accused of leading a faction of the powerful Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) and has allegedly been linked to the killing of a local mayor who had spoken out against organised crime, as well as the extortion of avocado producers.According to Reuters, the operation took place in Zapopan, in the western state of Jalisco, on November 8. Mexico's Navy said its special operations unit carried out the operation in coordination with the country's security ministry, following intelligence work by Mexico's National Intelligence Center and information shared by the DEA. Nineteen other people were detained alongside R2.The arrest is significant because the suspect was allegedly a key figure in the "Los Rs" criminal faction, which operates across Jalisco and neighbouring Michoacan. Mexican Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said the group was involved in extortion, drug trafficking, homicide, kidnapping, unlawful detention and attacks on security personnel. Its alleged victims included business owners and avocado producers.The arrest was not without violence. According to Mexico's Navy, its personnel came under armed attack during the operation and returned fire. R2 and one naval officer were wounded in the exchange and received medical attention. Authorities said the situation was brought under control.R2 had an outstanding arrest warrant in Mexico for aggravated homicide, as well as an arrest warrant connected to his extradition to the United States, Garcia Harfuch said. The DEA separately confirmed that he was wanted in the US on federal charges involving drug trafficking and firearms.Mexican authorities generally withhold the full surnames of criminal suspects in their official announcements, identifying them by their first name followed by "N". Consequently, the Navy's announcement identified the arrested man as Rafael "N", alias R2.One of the most serious allegations against R2 concerns the November 2025 killing of Carlos Manzo, the former mayor of Uruapan in Michoacan. The politician was shot dead during a public Day of the Dead celebration on November 1, while attending festivities with his family. Manzo, 40, had become known for openly challenging organised crime and demanding stronger action against the cartels operating in his municipality. Uruapan is a major centre of Mexico's avocado industry, and the surrounding region has repeatedly faced violence linked to criminal groups seeking control over agricultural businesses and transport networks.His killing shocked the country, particularly because it took place during a public celebration. A 17-year-old gunman shot Manzo, who later died in hospital. The attacker was subsequently killed by the mayor's security detail. Investigators believed other people had helped plan and facilitate the assassination.The investigation has since led to several arrests. In July 2026, Mexican authorities arrested another alleged Los Rs leader, Ramon Angel Alvarez Ayala, known as R1. Officials identified him as a suspected mastermind behind Manzo's assassination. R2's arrest is a separate development in the investigation and the wider crackdown on the faction. Following her husband's death, Manzo's wife, Grecia Quiroz, took over as mayor of Uruapan, pledging to continue his fight against organised crime.The allegations against Los Rs also draw attention to the criminal networks operating around Mexico's valuable avocado industry. Michoacan is one of the country's leading avocado-producing states, supplying domestic consumers as well as international markets. However, the industry's economic importance has made growers, transporters, traders and other businesses targets for organised crime.Cartels have allegedly used extortion, commonly referred to in Mexico as charging protection money, to extract payments from agricultural producers and businesses. Those who refuse to pay can face threats, kidnappings and violence. The criminal groups also seek influence over transportation routes and the movement of agricultural produce.Garcia Harfuch specifically identified avocado producers and business owners among the alleged victims of Los Rs. The group is also accused of involvement in drug trafficking, kidnappings and attacks on authorities across Jalisco and Michoacan.The pressure on agricultural communities has become a wider security concern. In October 2025, Bernardo Bravo, a prominent leader representing lemon producers in Michoacan, was also murdered. His killing highlighted the risks faced by agricultural leaders who speak out against extortion and organised crime.The latest arrest comes amid an ongoing campaign by Mexican authorities against the CJNG, one of the country's most powerful criminal organisations. Its operations extend across several Mexican states, with networks involved in drug trafficking, extortion and violence.The DEA's intelligence contribution to the Zapopan operation also highlights cooperation between Mexican and US authorities in targeting suspects accused of operating across borders. While Mexican investigators are pursuing the homicide allegations and domestic criminal charges, R2 is also wanted in the US on federal drug and firearms charges.
Article Summary: Rafael "N", known by the alias "R2", is accused of leading a faction of the powerful Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) He has allegedly been linked to the killing of a local mayor who had spoken out against organised crime, as well as the extortion of avocado producers. The operation took place in Zapopan, in the western state of Jalisco.

Article Title: At 17, Florida student Megan Markus founded a letter-writing project for incarcerated people; in 18 months, volunteers have sent more than 5,200 letters across all 50 US states and 105 countries and t
Article Text:
Florida teen's nonprofit sends thousands of letters to incarcerated people worldwide (Image Courtesy: Megan Markus via Points Of Light)

What inspired Megan to start Paper Wings Project?

How the letter-writing initiative works

Chrysalis Review gives incarcerated artists a platform

Why she believes human connection matters

A simple letter can offer something that people behind prison walls may go without for years: a reminder that they are not forgotten. In Florida, 17-year-old high school student Megan Markus has turned this idea into a global volunteer initiative, sending messages of hope and human connection to incarcerated people. Through her youth-led organisation, Paper Wings Project, she and a network of volunteers have sent more than 5,200 letters across all 50 US states and 105 countries and territories in just 18 months.Points of Light featured Markus in its Daily Point of Light series on November 5, 2026, recognising her efforts to connect with people in prisons through handwritten correspondence. The initiative also encourages recipients to write back, creating opportunities for personal conversations rather than one-way exchanges. What began as a way to combine her passion for writing with her interest in criminal justice has also led to a second initiative, Chrysalis Review, a literary and arts magazine that gives incarcerated writers and artists an opportunity to share their work.Growing up in Pinecrest, Florida, Markus was exposed to discussions about the criminal justice system through her parents, both of whom are criminal defence lawyers.These conversations made her aware of the challenges within the US justice system and its emphasis on punishment rather than rehabilitation. Writing had always been an important part of her life. She began looking for a way to connect her interest in language with her desire to support people affected by incarceration.About a year and a half ago, she established Paper Wings Project, a youth-led nonprofit that sends letters to people serving time in prisons. Her aim was to remind recipients that their voices and experiences matter, regardless of their circumstances. Markus believes that people should not be defined entirely by their criminal records. While she acknowledges that individuals must be held accountable for their actions, she also believes they deserve dignity, human connection and opportunities for personal expression.Paper Wings Project relies on volunteers who help write letters and respond to messages received from incarcerated individuals. For its work in the United States, the organisation searches state and federal prison databases to identify people who can receive correspondence. The first letter also encourages recipients to spread the word among other people in their facilities so that more individuals can participate.International outreach requires a different approach because many countries do not maintain publicly accessible databases of incarcerated people. In such cases, the organisation contacts prison officials directly and asks them to share information about the project and its invitation to contribute writing and artwork to Chrysalis Review. An important part of the initiative is its commitment to responding to everyone who writes back. Volunteers prepare personal replies, allowing recipients to become active participants in the correspondence.According to Markus, the responses have been among the most meaningful parts of the project. She recalled receiving a letter from someone who had not exchanged personal correspondence in 27 years. Others have shared how receiving a message made them feel valued and remembered.The success of Paper Wings Project inspired Markus to establish a second initiative called Chrysalis Review. It is a biannual literary and arts magazine dedicated to publishing creative work by incarcerated writers and artists. The publication gives people in prisons an opportunity to share their experiences, ideas, writing and artwork with a wider audience.Its first issue, titled Cocooned, was published in March 2026. The theme explored the difficult and often uncomfortable process of transformation, drawing inspiration from the dark, confined environment inside a butterfly's chrysalis. The organisation is working on its second issue, titled Breaking Free, which is expected to focus on reintegration and the challenges people face when returning to society.For Markus, the magazine is another way to ensure that incarcerated individuals have opportunities to express themselves rather than being defined only by their past actions.Markus has also faced questions about whether giving incarcerated people a platform means overlooking their crimes. Her response is that the project's purpose is not to judge their circumstances or excuse wrongdoing. Instead, she wants to recognise their humanity and provide space for personal expression. She believes that accountability and human dignity can exist together.The experience has also changed how she views volunteering. She describes it as a two-way relationship rather than an arrangement in which one person gives and another simply receives. The letters have affected the volunteers as much as they have helped recipients. Markus recalled reading some of the first responses with her father, an experience that moved both of them to tears.Through more than 5,200 letters and a growing creative platform, the teenager's initiative has created opportunities for people behind bars to communicate, share their stories and feel connected to the outside world. For Markus, every letter is a reminder that meaningful human connection can begin with a small act of kindness.
Article Summary: Megan Markus, 17, is a high school student from Pinecrest, Florida. She and a network of volunteers have sent more than 5,200 letters to incarcerated people in all 50 US states and 105 countries and territories in just 18 months. The initiative also encourages recipients to write back, creating opportunities for personal conversations rather than one-way exchanges. Markus has also established a second initiative, Chrysalis Review, a biannual literary and arts magazine dedicated to incarcerated writers and artists.

Article Title: 'Outrageous, ridiculous demands': US slams Iran as Tehran threatens to 'rain down hell'
Article Text:
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks to the press before departing for France from Homestead Air Reserve Base in Homestead, Florida. Rubio is traveling for the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting. AP/PTI(AP11_09_2026_000015B)

Araghchi warns US to accept Iran's proposal or face retaliation

US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Sunday said diplomatic efforts to end the conflict with Iran have hardly made any progress, accusing Tehran of putting forward demands that Washington considers unrealistic.Speaking to reporters at Homestead Air Reserve Base in Florida before leaving for Paris to attend the G7 Foreign Ministers' meeting, Rubio said several countries were continuing to mediate between the two sides but cautioned against expectations of an imminent breakthrough, ANI reported, citing Al Jazeera."You have a number of countries that continue to engage them with different ideas, but I wouldn’t say we’re at the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio said.He said President Donald Trump remained open to resolving the conflict through diplomacy, but argued that negotiations could not advance under the conditions being proposed by Iran."If there’s a chance to do it, we’ll explore it. Right now, it hasn’t been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic," Rubio said.Rubio's remarks came as Iranian foreign minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi asked Washington to accept Tehran's proposal to end the conflict on all fronts, warning of severe military retaliation if it chose to continue the war.In a post on X on Sunday, Araghchi said the decision now rested with the US administration following the midterm elections."American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own," he wrote.Araghchi said Iran's two-day proposal remained on the table, calling on Washington to meet its conditions, including an end to hostilities on all fronts."Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results. Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell," he added.Araghchi also acknowledged that diplomatic efforts to end the hostilities had reached an impasse, attributing the delay to the political situation in Washington following the US midterm elections."The main reason is the US election results, which have obviously come as a shock to everyone," he told reporters in Tehran, according to Al Jazeera.He said mediators would need time before they could resume their visits and efforts to facilitate negotiations.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Sunday said diplomatic efforts to end the conflict with Iran have hardly made any progress. Rubio said several countries were continuing to mediate between the two sides but cautioned against expectations of an imminent breakthrough.
