He said President Donald Trump remained open to resolving the conflict through diplomacy, but argued that negotiations could not advance under the conditions proposed by Iran.

Article Title: Whiskey dates & billion-dollar deals: How Nvidia boss Jensen Huang landed in Chinese spy scandal
Article Text:
Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen with reported connections across the global AI chip industry (Photo: Social Media/Daily Mail)

Also read:

What we know

Who is Alice Huang and what is Megaspeed's China connection?

What Jensen Huang said

What Jensen Huang wrote:

Alice Huang, a Chinese business executive suspected by US intelligence of working for Beijing, allegedly developed an intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, raising concerns that one of America's most influential technology executives may have been targeted in a Chinese espionage operation. Huang, is believed to have been recruited by China's intelligence apparatus to gather information about the billionaire and potentially influence his decisions on the global artificial intelligence industry.The allegations have placed the Nvidia chief, 63, under renewed scrutiny, with reports suggesting that US intelligence agencies had identified the suspected operation well before it became public.A report by the Financial Times said American officials had prepared a classified memo detailing the alleged romantic relationship. The development adds a new dimension to earlier revelations by The New York Times, which first reported that Huang had developed a close relationship with the Chinese businesswoman.Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen with reported connections across the global AI chip industry.According to the Daily Mail, the two allegedly became romantically involved, with US intelligence officials suspecting that the relationship could have been part of a Chinese espionage operation.The Financial Times reportedly revealed that American agencies had prepared a classified assessment of their alleged intimacy, which was circulated among a small group of senior government officials.Their association reportedly dates back to at least June 2024, when they were photographed together at a bar in Taipei following a technology trade show. Images shared on LinkedIn by technology company NetThunder showed Huang, wearing his trademark black leather jacket, sitting alongside Alice Huang during an evening gathering with industry executives. The two were reportedly seen drinking whiskey.They appeared together again in May 2025 at a dinner hosted by the Nvidia chief at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, a major technology exhibition. Photographs and livestream footage showed Alice Huang sitting close to him, kissing him on the cheek and putting her hand on his back. She was also seen following him when he stepped outside to speak to journalists. The two later left the restaurant in the same car.Alice Huang reportedly worked as a television journalist in China before moving into the technology sector. An online profile on a Chinese fund database, which AFP said it could not independently verify, listed previous employment at HSBC and Chinese broadcasters CCTV and Hunan TV.She later became a senior executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company that rents computing power to businesses for training and running AI systems. The company's website describes it as a core business partner of Nvidia's computing power cloud business in the Asia-Pacific region.According to the New York Times, Megaspeed had been under US government scrutiny since 2024 over suspicions that it was helping channel restricted Nvidia processors into China. Singapore authorities also reportedly questioned Alice Huang in 2025 as part of an investigation into the company.The Daily Mail reported that Megaspeed was spun off from a Chinese gaming company and expanded into AI data centres. The New York Times also reported that it had purchased more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over two years.Washington restricts exports of its most advanced AI processors to China over concerns that the technology could strengthen Beijing's military and technological capabilities. Megaspeed denied allegations of illegal chip transfers in December 2025, describing Bloomberg's reporting on the matter as misleading. Nvidia has also previously said its investigations found no evidence of wrongdoing.In his statement, the Nvidia chief apologised to his family for being unfaithful and said that the supported the independent investigation launched by the Nvidia board.To my colleagues at NVIDIA,I owe my family and all of you an apology.I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy.Jensen
Article Summary: Alice Huang, a Chinese business executive, allegedly developed an intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is believed to have been recruited by China's intelligence apparatus to gather information about the billionaire. The allegations have placed the Nvidia chief, 63, under renewed scrutiny, with reports suggesting that US intelligence agencies had identified the suspected operation.

Article Title: Jesse and Kylie Sebero manage more than 500 acres of Wisconsin forest for both timber and wildlife and open it to researchers; they are among five families shortlisted for the state’s $10,000 Leopold
Article Text:
Wisconsin family manages 500-acre forest for wildlife and timber; shortlisted for state conservation award (Image Credit: Sand County Foundation)

How the Seberos manage their 500-acre forest

Four other families shortlisted for the award

What is the Leopold Conservation Award?

A forest can be both a source of timber and a home for wildlife when it is managed with conservation in mind. In Wisconsin, Jesse and Kylie Sebero are demonstrating how privately owned woodland can support economic activity while protecting natural habitats. The couple manages more than 500 acres of contiguous forest in Marinette County, balancing timber production with wildlife conservation. They also open their property to researchers and organise educational tours for landowners and forestry professionals.The Sand County Foundation announced on September 10, 2026, that the Seberos were among five finalists for the 2026 Wisconsin Leopold Conservation Award. The $10,000 award recognises farmers and forestland owners who make significant efforts to protect soil health, water quality and wildlife habitat while managing productive land. The foundation, which announced the shortlist, presents the award with national sponsor American Farmland Trust and state partners Wisconsin Farm Bureau Federation and Dairy Farmers of Wisconsin. The winner is scheduled to be announced on November 12.The Sebero Family Tree Farm in Porterfield, Marinette County, covers more than 500 acres of contiguous forest. Rather than focusing only on timber production, the family considers the ecological and economic value of each acre.According to the Sand County Foundation, the Seberos manage the quality of timber and wildlife habitat across their property to achieve its fullest potential. Their approach reflects an effort to maintain a productive forest while ensuring that it continues to provide suitable habitat for wildlife. The family also makes the woodland available for research projects and tours. They welcome landowners, timber professionals and conservation experts who want to learn about forest management and conservation practices.Jesse Sebero's professional work further supports these efforts. He serves as a technical service provider for the US Department of Agriculture's Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS). In this role, he has written 272 forestry plans covering thousands of acres of privately owned land. His experience in providing technical guidance, together with the family's management of their own woodland, has made the Sebero property a place for research, learning and knowledge-sharing.The Seberos are competing with four other finalists whose conservation work focuses on farming, grazing, soil health and water protection. Andy Bensend of Dallas in Barron County has introduced cover crops, nutrient management and reduced tillage at AB Farms. Despite the shorter growing season in northern Wisconsin, he grows corn, soybeans and winter wheat while participating in research projects examining agricultural practices and soil health.The Brattset Family Farm in Jefferson County is managed by Weenonah Brattset and her daughter, Kirsten Jurcek. They have practised rotational grazing of beef cattle since 2005. Their work includes integrating cropland into perennial vegetation, improving soil health, water quality and biodiversity. They also work with the National Audubon Society to support grassland bird habitats and mentor other graziers.Jeff Endres, co-owner of Endres Berryridge Farms in Waunakee, Dane County, installed a manure composting facility to reduce the need for spreading manure during winter. He also founded the Yahara Pride farmer-led watershed group, which encourages farmers to adopt conservation practices and reduce phosphorus pollution in waterways.The Schoepp Family of Lodi, in Columbia and Sauk counties, uses no-till farming and diverse crop rotations to grow corn, soybeans, alfalfa and wheat. Their use of cover crops helps reduce soil erosion, improve soil structure and increase water infiltration. They also rotationally graze dairy heifers and beef cattle on cover crops.The Leopold Conservation Award is named after American conservationist Aldo Leopold, who promoted the idea of a land ethic in his influential 1949 book, A Sand County Almanac. His philosophy encouraged people to recognise their responsibility towards the land they own and manage. The award recognises farmers, ranchers and forestland owners who combine productive land management with efforts to improve the environment. Sand County Foundation and American Farmland Trust present the awards to private landowners across 28 states.In Wisconsin, the $10,000 award is presented with the support of the Wisconsin Farm Bureau Federation and Dairy Farmers of Wisconsin. An independent panel of agricultural and conservation leaders reviewed the applications and selected the five finalists. The first Wisconsin Leopold Conservation Award was presented in 2006 to woodland conservationist Gerry Mich of Appleton. The 2025 recipient was Michael Berg of Blanchardville in Lafayette County.The 2026 winner will be announced at the Wisconsin Board of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection meeting on November 12. For the Seberos, the nomination highlights how privately managed forests can serve several purposes at once, providing timber, supporting wildlife and creating opportunities for research and education.
Article Summary: Wisconsin family manages 500-acre forest for wildlife and timber; shortlisted for state conservation award. Jesse and Kylie Sebero are demonstrating how privately owned woodland can support economic activity while protecting natural habitats. The couple manages more than 500 acres of contiguous forest in Marinette County, balancing timber production with wildlife conservation.

Article Title: Her grandparents bought 146 acres in South Carolina in the 1940s; she promised her mother she would keep it together and has now barred future development on the family land
Article Text:
Smith and another landowner have protected over 250 acres of family land from development. (Representational photo)

How conservation easements protect land

Another family protects its century-old farm

Conservation agreements offer tax benefits

Families want others to consider the option

A woman in South Carolina has permanently protected her family's 146-acre property from future development, fulfilling a promise she made to her mother. Alice Smith placed the land, known as Duck Haven, in Pickens County under a conservation easement, a legal arrangement that restricts future construction while allowing the family to retain ownership.According to a report by WVLT 8, Smith's grandparents bought the property in the 1940s. She wanted to ensure that the land, which had remained with the family for generations, would not be sold or taken over for development. She said she had promised her mother that she would find a way to keep the property together. "I made a promise to my mother that I would find a way to keep the land together," Smith said as quoted by WVLT 8.The 146-acre property has rolling fields that connect to the Saluda River. It was mostly farmland when her grandparents purchased it, according to Smith. By choosing a conservation easement instead of accepting development offers, she has ensured that restrictions on future development will remain in place even after her lifetime.Smith is among two landowners in Upstate South Carolina who have recently protected more than 250 acres of family-owned land through conservation easements arranged with non-profit organisation Upstate Forever.The second property, Moore Farm, covers 110 acres in Greenville County and belongs to Ed Lomas's family.The organisation said the two agreements are part of its wider effort to protect land across the region. Upstate Forever now safeguards more than 40,000 acres across 10 counties.A conservation easement is a legal agreement that allows property owners to retain ownership while placing permanent restrictions on development. These restrictions continue to apply even if ownership of the property changes.Scott Park of Upstate Forever said landowners grant these restrictions to the organisation, which takes responsibility for ensuring that the agreed protections remain in place."Conservation easements, they’re in essence a charitable donation, so that’s why Upstate Forever can be a grantee of these conservation easements," Park said.He explained that the landowner grants the restrictions and the organisation becomes the long-term steward of the property."So the landowner is the grantor; they grant those restrictions to Upstate Forever. We are the forever steward, so we’re almost a partner in the pocket of that landowner now for as long as that landowner owns that piece of property."The second property covered by the agreements is Moore Farm, owned by the Lomas family for more than 100 years. The 110-acre farm is located near Horsepen Creek in Greenville County.The property was previously used to grow cotton. Since around the 1950s, it has been used to raise cattle. However, new residential neighbourhoods have gradually developed around the farm.Ed Lomas said the change has been particularly noticeable in the traffic passing through the area. "Twenty years ago, you would wait for cars to come by maybe every few minutes," Lomas said. "Now it’s a constant stream, especially first thing in the morning."The process of securing the conservation easement took around a year and a half. Lomas said he decided to protect the farm after hearing about another family that was struggling to hold on to its property.He recalled receiving a call from a family friend whose relatives were getting older and could no longer manage their land. They were concerned about leaving the property to their children and the difficulties that could follow. "I actually had a phone call from a family friend about a year ago saying they had exactly that scenario," Lomas said.He said the family believed selling the property was their only option. "They were older, they couldn’t take care of it, it was going to be left to the children, it was going to be a big mess. They felt that was their only option, just to sell the land."Lomas wanted to prevent his own family from facing similar pressure. He said the agreement would protect the farm and ensure that his children would not be pressured into selling it for development. "I know it’ll be safe and the kids will not be able to be pressured into selling it as a development," he said.Conservation easements can also provide financial benefits to property owners because they are treated as charitable donations.According to the South Carolina Farm Bureau, the value of an easement is calculated by comparing the property's fair market value before and after the development restrictions are imposed. The difference is recognised by the Internal Revenue Service as a non-cash charitable donation. Landowners can claim this amount as a federal tax deduction for up to 15 years.South Carolina also offers state tax credits, generally amounting to a maximum of $250 per acre. These credits have no expiration date and can be applied towards the landowner's personal income.In addition, many easements qualify for direct financial support from sources such as the South Carolina Conservation Bank. This funding is generally calculated as a percentage of the easement's value and paid to the landowner at closing.Park said Upstate Forever was seeing growing interest from landowners who wanted to protect their properties against development.He said families such as the Lomas and Smith families were determined to preserve land that had remained in their families for generations."You meet landowners like Ed and Alice that are just salt of the earth," Park said. "They just want to protect their property. They see the development pressure that’s coming around them and they are pretty much, they are laser focused on getting these properties protected, and we’re happy to be a partner in that."Both landowners said they hoped their decisions would encourage other families to explore ways to protect their properties."There are opportunities and ways to protect and conserve the property you may have," Lomas said. Smith said she did not consider herself wealthy or well-connected but wanted others to know that protecting family land was possible."I’m not well-to-do, I’m not really well connected, but if for some reason I can plant a seed in anyone, that if I’m able to do this, they can too," she said.For Smith, the agreement means that her family's land will remain protected even after she is gone. She said she wanted to ensure that the work and sacrifices made by earlier generations were not lost to development."What your family sacrificed and worked so hard for did not go to waste and a developer is not going to be able to ever touch it, and even when I’m gone, it’s still going to stay like this," she said.
Article Summary: Alice Smith and another landowner have protected over 250 acres of family land from development. A conservation easement is a legal agreement that allows property owners to retain ownership while placing permanent restrictions on development. Smith's grandparents bought the property in the 1940s and she wanted to ensure it would not be sold or taken over for development.

Article Title: South Carolina father leaves his 6-year-old daughter sleeping outside Target with a pillow and blanket to hold his place in a queue for Pokemon cards; arrested after customers alert police
Article Text:
Father left daughter alone to retain his place in the queue

Customers alert police after child is left unattended

Father charged with unlawful conduct toward a child

Pokemon card release draws overnight crowds

A 35-year-old man in South Carolina has been arrested after allegedly leaving his six-year-old daughter sleeping outside a Target store in the middle of the night while he went home to hold his place in a queue for Pokemon trading cards. According to the Charleston Police Department, John-Michael Dooley gave the child a pillow and blanket before leaving her unattended. He reportedly stayed away for around an hour, prompting concerned customers waiting outside the store to contact police. Officers arrived at the scene at approximately 2.30 am on November 6. The girl was found unharmed, while Dooley was subsequently arrested and charged with unlawful conduct toward a child.The incident took place outside a Target store in West Ashley, a neighbourhood in Charleston, South Carolina, as customers gathered overnight for the release of a new Pokemon trading card collection.Police said Dooley had brought his young daughter to the store and left her sleeping outside with a pillow and blanket. He then went home, allegedly to ensure he did not lose his position in the queue.According to the police account, Dooley later admitted to detectives that he had left the child unattended so he could maintain his place in line and avoid missing the opportunity to purchase the cards.Other customers waiting outside the store became concerned when they realised the six-year-old had been left without adult supervision.After Dooley failed to return for approximately an hour, witnesses contacted the police. Officers arrived at around 2.30 am on November 6, and the customers identified Dooley when he eventually returned to the store.The child was found unharmed. Following the incident, she was placed in emergency protective custody with the South Carolina Department of Social Services.Dooley was arrested and charged with unlawful conduct toward a child. He was subsequently held at the Al Cannon Detention Center in Charleston County.According to reports, his bond was set at US$40,000, with an initial court appearance scheduled for December 18, 2026.The queue had formed for the release of the Pokemon Trading Card Game collection Mega Evolution – Delta Reign, which went on sale on November 6.The launch attracted collectors and enthusiasts who gathered outside retail stores to purchase the new cards. Individual packs reportedly started at around US$5, with demand contributing to overnight queues.
Article Summary: John-Michael Dooley, 35, charged with unlawful conduct toward a child. Incident took place outside a Target store in Charleston, South Carolina. Customers had gathered overnight for the release of a new Pokemon trading card collection. Dooley allegedly left the child unattended so he could hold his place in the queue.

Article Title: 'He probably has an excuse': Trump reacts to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Chinese spy scandal
Article Text:
Trump still called the CEO 'honourable guy'

US president Donald Trump on Sunday reacted to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admission to having an affair with alleged Chines spy Alice Huang. Trump claimed that Huang "probably had an excuse" and that he was an "honourable guy"On being asked if the US president had talked to the CEO, Trump denied adding that, "I have not spoken to him about it, I just know he's a fine person. You never know what's going on. I hope everything's fine, he's done such an incredible job. He's a fine person in my opinion.""I think he's an honorable guy, I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it. He's done an amazing job for the country," he added.Also read: Rubio warned Trump admin about Nvidia CEO's alleged ties to Alice Huang - Report Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, apologising to his family and colleagues in a letter to employees. He said he took “full responsibility” for his actions and acknowledged that he had fallen short of the responsibility that came with leading the company.“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Huang wrote.He added: “Leading Nvidia is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility.”Huang did not name Alice Huang in the letter or directly address reports about her alleged links to Chinese intelligence. However, he said he supported the Nvidia board's investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation and would cooperate fully.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump on Sunday reacted to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admission to having an affair with alleged Chines spy Alice Huang. Trump claimed that Huang "probably had an excuse" and that he was an "honourable guy" On being asked if the US president had talked to the CEO, Trump denied adding that, "I have not spoken to him about it"

Article Title: ‘Some days better than others’: Joe Biden’s memoir promotion to be limited amid cancer battle
Article Text:
Ex-US President Joe Biden’s ‘painful’ prostate cancer ‘spread into his bones and further’.

Former US President Joe Biden has said his battle with prostate cancer will limit the number of promotional appearances he can make for his upcoming memoir, "Promise Me, America", which is due to be released on November 17.“Some days are better than others. It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down,” Biden, 83, wrote on social media on Sunday. He said he would not be able to take part in as many conversations about the book as he had hoped, but added that he was hopeful “the words on the page speak for themselves”.Biden’s publisher announced the memoir on July 15. The book is described as his personal account of his four years in the White House, covering his presidency, his decision to seek a second term and his eventual withdrawal from the 2024 presidential race.The 480-page memoir is expected to cover his administration’s response to the Covid-19 pandemic, the January 6 Capitol attack, the economy, infrastructure and healthcare, as well as US foreign policy and its support for Ukraine. It will also offer Biden’s account of the decision to step aside from the presidential contest. The title echoes his 2017 memoir, Promise Me, Dad, which focused on the death of his son Beau.Biden's health has remained a concern since he disclosed his prostate cancer diagnosis in May 2025, less than four months after leaving office. His office said the cancer had a Gleason score of 9, indicating an aggressive form of the disease, and had already spread to his bones. It also said the cancer appeared to be hormone-sensitive, making it possible to manage with treatment.Biden underwent radiation therapy and hormone treatment. In September 2026, he said the radiation treatment had “worked as intended” and that his doctors had helped bring the disease under control. He did not say he was cancer-free.However, his son Hunter Biden offered a account of his condition in an interview with the BBC in August. He said the cancer had “metastasized into his bones and further”, describing it as painful and debilitating.“It’s really sad to watch,” Hunter said, adding that he wished his father would “complain more” about his health because “it’s not good”.Biden, who turns 84 on November 20, said when the memoir was announced in July that he had been spending time with his family and receiving treatment for cancer. “I’m dealing with a cancer diagnosis, been getting treatment, and it’s going really well,” he said at the time.
Article Summary: Ex-US President Joe Biden's new memoir, "Promise Me, America," is due to be released on November 17. The book is described as his personal account of his four years in the White House. Biden, 83, said he would not be able to take part in as many conversations about the book as he had hoped.

Article Title: In 1943, U.S. Army Air Corps Captain David Fransen mailed his five-year-old daughter a coconut from the Philippines; he carved a smiling face on it and wrote her address on the shell
Article Text:
A representative AI image of a soldier in the middle of World War carving a smiling face into a coconut. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

A coconut became an unusual message from the Philippines

Wartime correspondence carried emotional importance

During World War II, Captain David Fransen creatively sent a carved coconut to his daughter. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

A small wartime object became part of historical preservation

Between the Second World War and modern times, many military men and women were separated from their loved ones by vast distances. They sent letters and packages back and forth, but sometimes a service member wanted to keep communication simple and personal. US Army Air Corps Captain David Fransen was stationed in the Philippines in 1943. He wanted to tell his five-year-old daughter that he loved her. He carved a coconut with a smile on it, and then sent it through the mail to his daughter, so she would have a keepsake from her father.According to Chapman University’s Leatherby Libraries , Captain David Fransen was in the Philippines. He came up with a unique way to communicate with his daughter, Susan. Instead of simply mailing a letter, he sent a coconut. He etched a smiley face on the shell and addressed it with the five-year-old's mailing information, creating the shipping capsule for his palm-sized message.The gesture showed the ingenuity with which servicemen were able to connect with their loved ones through the conflict. Fransen's choice of a coconut made the message especially memorable. It also made the message unique because the coconut could carry both a personal decoration and the information needed for delivery.For a young girl waiting for news of her father, the coconut must have been a memorable reminder.The coconut was among the wartime correspondence later highlighted by the University Centre of American War Letters archive, which collects personal letters and other written records from American servicemen and women, preserving accounts that provide a more intimate understanding of military history. Fransen's coconut stood out because it demonstrated that communication did not always have to take the form of conventional paper letters.Fransen's unusual piece of mail was a part of a larger story of connection between American soldiers abroad and their families. In the Second World War, millions of servicemen and women served overseas and were often separated from loved ones for months or even years. Letters provided one of the main means of sharing information, staying in touch, and reassuring loved ones about family affairs. The amount of mail posed serious problems for the service post office space, with floods of correspondence. The US military devised Victory Mail, or V-Mail, in 1942. It photographed handwritten notes on microfilm for overseas movement, where they were reproduced on smaller sheets of paper.A study in war in history examined how postcards shaped relationships between civilians and military personnel during World War I. Although the study focused on a different form of communication, it highlights how written messages helped maintain connections across great distances. The coconut offered a more unusual way to achieve the same purpose. Rather than sending an ordinary letter or postcard, he chose an object that reflected the environment in which he was serving. The carved, grinning face gave the coconut a personal touch, while the address written on its shell turned it into an unconventional means of communication. Chapman University's 2015 exhibition drew new attention to his coconut during a celebration of the 70th anniversary of the conclusion of the Second World War. The exhibit, World War 2: The Pacific Theatre, featured letters from American service members who had fought throughout the Pacific. The correspondence was displayed alongside other wartime letters chronicling the experiences of those often broken apart from their loved ones by duty. The archive was formed to collect and maintain correspondence from different times in American military history, providing historians with the type of material that is usually absent from the official record.
Article Summary: US Army Air Corps Captain David Fransen was stationed in the Philippines in 1943. He wanted to tell his five-year-old daughter that he loved her. He carved a smiley face on the shell and sent it through the mail. The gesture showed the ingenuity with which servicemen were able to connect with their loved ones.

Article Title: An Ohio man bought a house before marriage and later rented it to his brother; after divorce, an appeals court kept the property his alone and upheld $20,000 in legal fees against his wife
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI-generated)

How the property became part of the divorce dispute

Why the court considered the house his separate property

Why the wife was ordered to pay $20,000 in legal fees

Appeals court upholds the original decision

A house purchased before marriage can become a point of dispute during divorce, particularly when a couple has lived in the property and mortgage payments are later made through a joint bank account. In Ohio, a divorce case involving a property bought by a husband six years before his marriage raised questions about whether rental income and financial contributions during the marriage had changed its ownership status. The man had later rented the house to his brother, who continued paying rent while the couple was married.In a November 6, 2026, decision , the Ohio Court of Appeals, First District, upheld the husband's ownership of the property and an order requiring his former wife to pay $20,000 towards his attorney fees. The ruling came in Ellison v. Ellison, case number C-260069, with the judgment available on Justia. The court found that the husband had sufficiently traced the rental income, which exceeded the property's mortgage payments, and that the trial court had properly considered the wife's conduct during the divorce proceedings when awarding legal fees.Stephen Ellison purchased a house on Elbrook Avenue in August 2012, six years before marrying Sherrun Ellison on September 1, 2018.The couple lived there from around September 2017 until August or September 2018, around the time of their marriage.After they moved out, Stephen rented the property to his brother and his brother's wife. According to his testimony, the initial monthly rent was $850, which later increased to $1,000 and eventually $1,500 in 2023. When Sherrun filed for divorce in May 2023, the ownership of the house became one of the unresolved issues. She argued that the property should be treated as marital property because money from their joint bank account had been used to pay its mortgage.She also maintained that the couple had contributed to the property's upkeep during their marriage. Their claimed contributions included replacing the carpet and stove, painting the interior and paying for regular maintenance. However, Stephen disputed these claims. He said the improvements had been completed and paid for before the marriage and that the rental income from his brother covered the mortgage payments.During the divorce proceedings, Stephen presented a lease agreement with his brother and bank statements showing deposits and transfers that he said came from rental payments. He explained that his brother and sister-in-law paid rent through cash, checks and payment applications. He deposited the money into his personal bank account and then used it to pay the mortgage or transferred it into the couple's joint account to cover the payments.His brother also testified that he and his wife had rented the house since 2017, initially paying $850 a month plus utilities. He confirmed that the rent increased over time and that they eventually paid the full amount, even when payments were sometimes delayed.The trial court accepted their testimony and found that the rental income exceeded the mortgage payments. It also concluded that no marital money or labour had been used for improvements or maintenance that would create a marital interest in the property. The court therefore classified the entire Elbrook property as Stephen's separate property.The divorce also involved a separate dispute over attorney fees. Stephen argued that his former wife's actions had increased the cost and duration of the proceedings. His lawyer testified that he had accumulated $56,328 in attorney fees over approximately two years of litigation, excluding trial fees. She described several issues that required additional legal work, including changes in legal representation, withdrawn settlement agreements and disputes involving the children and property.The trial court ordered Sherrun to contribute $20,000 towards those expenses. It considered her conduct during the proceedings and found that some of her actions had unnecessarily prolonged the case. Sherrun challenged the award, arguing that the court had relied on statements made during settlement negotiations and had not properly considered Stephen's own conduct. She also argued that the fee award was punitive.The appeals court rejected these arguments. It explained that Ohio law allows courts to award reasonable attorney fees in divorce cases when doing so is equitable. Judges can consider the parties' financial circumstances and their behaviour during litigation. The court also clarified that a judge does not have to establish serious misconduct before awarding legal fees. A party's conduct can be considered when it unnecessarily increases the time and expense of resolving a divorce.The Ohio appeals court found no reason to overturn the lower court's findings. It concluded that the evidence supported Stephen's claim that rental income covered the mortgage and that the house had retained its status as his separate property. It also upheld the $20,000 attorney-fee award, finding that the trial court had appropriately considered the circumstances of the divorce proceedings. The November 6 decision affirmed the original judgment, leaving both the property classification and the attorney-fee order unchanged.The ruling highlights how a property purchased before marriage can retain its separate status when its owner can establish the source of mortgage payments and show that marital contributions did not create an ownership interest. It also demonstrates that courts can consider how spouses conduct themselves during divorce proceedings when deciding whether one should contribute to the other's legal expenses.
Article Summary: Ohio man bought a house in 2012, six years before his marriage. He later rented it to his brother, who continued paying rent while the couple was married. When Sherrun filed for divorce in May 2023, the ownership of the house became one of the unresolved issues. She argued that the property should be treated as marital property because money from their joint bank account had been used to pay its mortgage. The court found that the husband had sufficiently traced the rental income, which exceeded the property's mortgage payments, and that the trial court had properly considered the wife's conduct during the divorce.

Article Title: Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans faceless anti-terror courts: Report
Article Text:
Faceless terror courts, Rs 70bn police boost planned in Pakistan’s KP (Reuters photo)

Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province plans to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts to protect witnesses, prosecutors and judges involved in terrorism cases, according to a report by Dawn on Sunday.The provincial administration also plans to allocate 70 billion Pakistani rupees annually to the police and Counter-Terrorism Department to strengthen their capabilities, the report said.The developments come less than a month after Pakistan's federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, accusing the provincial government led by former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) of failing to engage in the fight against terrorism.Under the move, the chief minister and provincial cabinet ceased to hold office, with Governor Faisal Karim Kundi assuming executive authority with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council.Both the national assembly and senate approved the emergency on October 14, while a joint sitting of Parliament endorsed the emergency and governor's rule the following day.At a televised briefing on Sunday, Home Secretary Amjad Ali Khan said an amendment had been sent to establish faceless anti-terrorism courts.He said witnesses were reluctant to testify in terrorism cases because of fears for their safety. The proposed system would also protect prosecutors and judges, *Dawn* quoted him as saying.Khan said the administration planned to allocate 59.8 billion Pakistani rupees to the police and 10.3 billion Pakistani rupees to the Counter-Terrorism Department, with funds earmarked for infrastructure and equipment.The plans also include strengthening police stations and checkpoints, expanding the Safe City project and installing anti-drone systems in Dera Ismail Khan, Lakki Marwat and Bannu, the report said.Khan said the province faced a shortage of more than 10,000 police personnel and lacked adequate security infrastructure, particularly in the merged districts. He also flagged weak counter-drone capabilities, noting that militants were increasingly using drone technology.The administration plans to intensify intelligence-based operations, arrest terrorist facilitators, re-verify people placed on Pakistan's Fourth Schedule and mobilise the Rapid Response Force, Khan said.It also plans to deploy artificial intelligence tools to monitor social media and counter terrorist narratives, while satellite communication systems will be installed in areas with inadequate connectivity.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governor Kundi, who attended the briefing, said restoring peace and strengthening the police were the administration's priorities. He said development could follow only after security was restored and called for greater political ownership of the fight against terrorism.Kundi said the police would be provided with weapons, ammunition and other resources, while facilities in the merged districts would also be improved. He said groups taking up arms against the state could not be offered dialogue and would be dealt with accordingly, Dawn reported.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province plans to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts to protect witnesses, prosecutors and judges involved in terrorism cases. The provincial administration also plans to allocate 70 billion Pakistani rupees annually to the police and Counter-Terrorism Department.

Article Title: Balochistan Parties call statewide shutdown in mid-November as crisis deepens in troubled province
Article Text:
(Representative image) (Photo: ANI).

Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19, to be followed by demonstrations at district headquarters. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns.The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP) at the Quetta Press Club, according to a report by The Express Tribune cited by ANI. ANP provincial president Asghar Khan Achakzai chaired the meeting, which was attended by representatives of the National Party, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, Pashtunkhwa National Awami Party and several other political groups. The participants agreed to bring their joint political and democratic efforts under a coordinated movement to raise public grievances.In a joint declaration, the parties described the situation in Balochistan as alarming. They cited persistent insecurity, terrorism, extremism, armed group activities, targeted killings and kidnappings for ransom. They also raised the unresolved issue of missing persons, and highlighted the difficulties faced by transporters and passengers travelling on national highways.The parties pointed to rising unemployment and economic decline. They blamed the closure of trade and transit routes with Afghanistan and Iran for disrupting economic activity across the province. Soaring inflation, prolonged power and gas outages, petroleum levies and restrictions on the supply of essential agricultural inputs, including urea fertiliser, were also cited. According to The Express Tribune, the leaders said these issues had adversely affected agriculture, trade, industries and employment.The participating parties also criticised the provincial and federal governments, accusing them of failing to ensure public safety, maintain law and order, protect natural resources and restore economic stability.Furthermore, the parties announced a provincial-level meeting on November 26 to decide the next course of action. An all-parties conference will be held in the first week of December to take Balochistan’s concerns to the national leadership.
Article Summary: Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns. The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP)

Article Title: 'If he wishes to come’: Pakistan open to considering visa for Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s Lahore visit
Article Text:
पंजाब सीएम भगवंत मान

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann should visit Pakistan for the World Punjabi Conference? Yes, it would promote cultural ties. No, travel could be risky. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Pakistan has indicated its willingness to grant a visa to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should he wish to visit the neighbouring country for the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27, following an invitation to the event.Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing while responding to a question about Mann's possible visit, PTI reported."The government would consider issuing Mann a visa if he wishes to visit Pakistan. However, whether the Indian government permits him to travel is an entirely separate matter," he told reporters in Islamabad.On October 23, Mann had said that he had received an invitation to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore.However, the Punjab chief minister also raised doubts over whether he would be permitted to travel to Pakistan.“Our culture is the same. Many poets from here will go there,” he remarked.Mann had also voiced his wish for all members of the Punjab legislative assembly to visit Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan if it reopened.The corridor, which links Dera Baba Nanak in Punjab with the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan, was established to facilitate Sikh pilgrims visiting the shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.It enables Indian pilgrims to visit the gurdwara without a Pakistani visa, subject to applicable arrangements.The corridor has remained closed to pilgrims travelling from the India since May 7, 2025, when India launched pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22.Last month, the Centre denied political clearance to Mann for his visit to Paris, prompting the Punjab government to challenge the decision before the Punjab and Haryana high court.The high court subsequently cleared his visit, observing that the Centre had “not explained” the political considerations it cited while refusing permission for his trip to the French capital.
Article Summary: Pakistan has indicated its willingness to grant a visa to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should he wish to visit the neighbouring country for the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27. Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing.

Article Title: Pakistan’s forex rises by record $ 110 million in just a week despite West Asia crisis
Article Text:
Pakistan’s central bank reported a $110 million weekly rise in foreign exchange reserves, taking total holdings to a record $26.864 billion

Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $110 million in a week to a record $26.864 billion, according to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), even as the West Asia conflict continues to disrupt global energy markets and push up oil prices.In a statement on Thursday, the central bank said the country's total reserves had increased from $26.754 billion in the previous week.The rise included a $39 million increase in SBP-held reserves, while commercial banks' foreign exchange holdings also improved.The SBP said Pakistan's reserves had increased by $5 billion since the conflict began in February. Its own holdings rose from $16.568 billion in February to $21.568 billion as of October 30. The central bank said the improved reserve position had helped stabilise the exchange rate and provided exporters with confidence to repatriate their earnings without delay.However, Pakistan continues to face a substantial trade gap. Its trade deficit stood at $14.6 billion in the first four months of FY27, with imports at $26 billion against exports of $11.4 billion. Financial analysts have attributed the stability of the Pakistani rupee and the improvement in foreign exchange availability largely to rising remittances.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $110 million in a week to a record $26.864 billion, according to the State Bank of Pakistan. The rise included a $39 million increase in SBP-held reserves. The SBP said Pakistan's reserves had increased by $5 billion since the conflict began in February.

Article Title: How deep is Pakistan's debt dependence on China? The numbers tell the story
Article Text:
China leads as external debt touches $135 billion

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Pakistan rely more on multilateral institutions for financial aid? Yes, it's safer No, seek private investors 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s external debt has nearly doubled over the past decade, climbing to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $68.67 billion in 2015, according to a World Bank report cited by Dawn.The figures underline the Islamic country’s growing dependence on foreign borrowing to meet its financial needs.The debt stock comprised $107.07 billion in public and publicly guaranteed loans, $17.58 billion in private non-guaranteed debt and $10.45 billion in short-term borrowing.Of the public debt, multilateral institutions accounted for the largest share at $56.83 billion. Pakistan also owed $42.43 billion to bilateral lenders and $7.8 billion to private creditors.China remained Pakistan’s biggest individual creditor, with outstanding loans of $22.4 billion. The World Bank was next with $19.2 billion, followed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to which Pakistan owed $16.83 billion.The report also highlighted the difference in borrowing costs. Loans from official creditors had an average maturity of 16 years, a four-year grace period and an interest rate of 3.6%. Private credit, in contrast, came at a much steeper average interest rate of 8.6%, with a repayment period of three years and a grace period of just one year.Across the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region, debt-service and interest ratios showed improvement.However, the region’s external debt-to-gross national income (GNI) ratio rose from 26.7% to 29.4% in 2025. This was the sharpest annual increase recorded by any region, pointing to a continued build-up of external debt.Pakistan also received some relief through fresh financing and loan extensions during the year. China extended the maturity of $2 billion in loans, while the International Monetary Fund (IMF) disbursed $2.3 billion under its Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility programmes, aimed at supporting the country’s longer-term economic stability.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s external debt has nearly doubled over the past decade, climbing to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $68.67 billion in 2015. Of the public debt, multilateral institutions accounted for the largest share at $56.83 billion. Pakistan also owed $42.43 billion to bilateral lenders and $7.8 billion to private creditors.

Article Title: 11 dead, 33 injured in devastating bus-truck collision in eastern Pakistan
Article Text:
.

At least 11 people were killed and 33 others injured after a passenger bus collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan on Thursday, police and rescue officials said.The accident occurred in Pakpattan district of Punjab province, AP reported, citing hospital official Dr Ahmad Raza. Rescue teams used cranes and other heavy machinery to pull passengers trapped inside the wreckage. The operation lasted nearly three hours, police said.Authorities declared an emergency at the hospital and called in additional doctors and medical personnel to treat the injured, Raza said.Pakistan president Asif Ali Zardari expressed grief over the deaths in a statement, shared on social media, while also extending his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.“Extending his best wishes for the speedy recovery of the injured, he directed the relevant authorities to continue providing all possible support for medical treatment and relief operations,” the statement added.Road accidents are common in Pakistan, where poor road conditions, inadequate enforcement of traffic regulations and unsafe driving practices contribute to frequent collisions. Last month, at least 12 people were killed and around two dozen others injured after a bus collided with a van in the southwestern province of Balochistan, according to AP.
Article Summary: A bus collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan, police and rescue officials say. Rescue teams used cranes and other heavy machinery to pull passengers trapped inside the wreckage. Pakistan president Asif Ali Zardari expresses grief over the deaths. Road accidents are common in Pakistan, where poor road conditions contribute to frequent collisions.

Article Title: Where Is Bashir Zeb Baloch? Mystery mounts after BLA announces leadership change
Article Text:
BLA announces Bashir Zeb Baloch’s exit as chief, while unverified reports swirl over his whereabouts and possible death (Image credit: X posts)

NEW DELHI: Mystery shrouds the status and whereabouts of Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Commander-in-Chief Bashir Zeb Baloch, following an announcement by the rebel group on Tuesday that he was stepping down from his post. The announcement stood in contrast to claims circulating on pro-Pakistan military social media accounts that suggest an assassination attempt or his death.Rumours across pro-Pakistan Telegram channels, citing unnamed sources, speculated that Zeb was the target of a poisoning attempt by a close confidant in Kandahar and was subsequently rushed to a military hospital.Other accounts went further, claiming he was eliminated in a Pakistani military airstrike inside Afghanistan in September — a claim that remains independently unverified.Zeb had emerged as the primary face of the BLA's major offensive, Operation Herof. Visuals released during the operation depicting him riding a motorcycle without security cover had created significant ripples across security and intelligence circles.In an official statement issued by the BLA, the group clarified the context around Zeb's departure saying: "Following the decision of the Senior Command Council in accordance with the constitution of the organization, former Commander-in-Chief of the Baloch Liberation Army, Bashir Zeb Baloch, will no longer serve as the head of the organization.""Until the selection of a new Commander-in-Chief, all administrative, military, and policy-making powers have been officially entrusted to the Senior Command Council, the highest supreme body of the BLA, while military operations across all fronts will continue without interruption," the statement from BLA said.The rebel group saidnthat during the reorganization of the BLA in 2018, the ideological and structural founder of the BLA, Ustad Aslam Baloch, had brought an end to hereditary politics and lifelong leadership, establishing the organization on the foundations of merit, transparency, and institutional principles."He set the guiding principle that no matter how influential, prominent, or high-ranking a commander may be in this movement, no individual can remain Commander-in-Chief for life. To maintain this ideological and organizational continuity, a clear and consensus-based procedure was incorporated into the BLA constitution so that, if the need ever arose, an established and peaceful constitutional pathway for a smooth leadership transition would exist. ""In accordance with this principle, a joint meeting of the highest bodies of the BLA was held on October 16, during which constitutional and organizational matters were thoroughly reviewed. During the meeting, all commanders unanimously decided in favor of leadership transition to impart fresh momentum to the organization's activities," the statement said."Our operational activities across all fronts continue without interruption. The name of the new Commander-in-Chief will be announced soon at the conclusion of the next phases," the BLA said.
Article Summary: Mystery shrouds the status and whereabouts of Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Commander-in-Chief Bashir Zeb Baloch. Zeb had emerged as the primary face of the BLA's major offensive, Operation Herof. Unverified reports suggest an assassination attempt or his death.

Article Title: Asim Munir flags growing Hindu-Jewish ties threat to Pakistan and Muslim world, reveals Iran
Article Text: Iran's senior security official Mohsen Rezaei has claimed that Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir warned of growing ties between Hindus and Jews, alleging that the emerging partnership posed a threat to Pakistan and the wider Muslim world.In an interview with Iranian state media, Rezaei said Munir raised concerns over growing India-Israel ties during a four-nation security meeting in Tehran on October 26. The meeting was attended by Munir, Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi defence minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Rezaei, who represented Iran.Rezaei also claimed that the leaders shared concerns that Israel could target other countries in the region after Iran."They spoke very strongly against Israel. Mr Khalid bin Salman said that after you (Iran), Israel would target Turkey, and then come after Saudi Arabia," Rezaei said during the interview."Mr Ibrahim Kalin, the head of Turkish intelligence, shared the same view. Mr Asim Munir also spoke about the threat posed by Israel and the emerging bond between Hindus and Jews against Muslims and even Pakistan. These remarks reflect their information and concerns about how Israel may act towards them in the future," he added.Munir has repeatedly invoked religious differences between Hindus and Muslims, describing the two communities as fundamentally distinct.Days before the Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, Munir had spoken about the differences between Hindus and Muslims in their religion, customs, traditions, thoughts and ambitions. He had also invoked the Two-Nation Theory.While Rezaei's latest account of Munir's remarks remains unverified, the reported comments are consistent with the Pakistani army chief's earlier rhetoric.Meanwhile, India and Israel have steadily expanded cooperation across defence, intelligence, counterterrorism, trade, agriculture, water management and emerging technologies. The two countries elevated their relationship to a Special Strategic Partnership during PM Narendra Modi's visit to Israel in February 2026.Israel had also openly backed India's right to self-defence during Operation Sindoor against Pakistan in May 2025. Israeli Ambassador to India Reuven Azar had said that terrorists had nowhere to hide.In February this year, Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu proposed a "hexagon of alliances" involving India, Israel, Greece, Cyprus and other countries to counter what he described as radical Shia and Sunni axes.In October, Netanyahu again named India as a key partner in his plans to build alternative alliances. He also warned that Israel could face a hostile US administration after President Donald Trump leaves the White House.
Article Summary: Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir raised concerns over growing India-Israel ties during a four-nation security meeting in Tehran on October 26. Munir, Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi defence minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Rezaei, who represented Iran.

Article Title: 'America taking its place': Shehbaz's rival Fazlur Rehman accuses Asim Munir of sabotaging ties with China
Article Text: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Monday accused Pakistan army of derailing Chinese investments under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor ( CPEC ), alleging that the country's mineral wealth was being used to advance foreign interests and facilitate a shift towards United States.In a social media post on X, Rehman claimed that Pakistan had disappointed Beijing by halting CPEC-linked investments midway and warned that the loss of Chinese confidence could deter other countries from investing in Pakistan."You have disappointed China, you have halted their investment midway, and when China is disappointed, the rest of the world will not come to invest in your country either," he said.He alleged that the US was stepping in to fill the space left by China, claiming that American officials had acknowledged this to him."And who is taking China's place? America is taking its place. This has been admitted by the Americans themselves in front of me," he said.Rehman clarified that he was not opposed to foreign investment in Pakistan's mineral sector, saying the country urgently needed international capital, development projects and economic opportunities."We do not disagree with the principle of investment from around the world here.Multinational companies come, they invest; America is not immune to this, Russia is not immune, China is not immune, Britain and France are not immune," he said."And who is taking China's place? America is taking its place. This has been admitted by the Americans themselves in front of me, and our esteemed elders here have taken those beautiful, beautiful stones to their offices and presented them, and the ambassador they have here at the time has also said it in her interview," he added.The JUI-F chief also alleged that politicians backed by the military establishment prioritised their personal interests and the demands of their patrons over Pakistan's economic well-being."These Pakistani politicians - whose priorities I know - in all such matters, they first determine their own share, and only then do they think about the country," he said.Fazlur Rehman also questioned the imposition of governor's rule and the declaration of an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, alleging that the measures were linked to concerns over the region's mineral reserves."On what grounds? Terrorism? The provincial government is aligned with the narrative of terrorism; it is the federation that is not providing support for that narrative," he said.He further alleged that the focus on terrorism had subsequently disappeared from the debate, while discussions surrounding mineral reserves had also been dropped."As soon as governor's rule was imposed and as soon as the emergency was declared, the topic of terrorism simply vanished, and from their side, the discussion of mineral reserves was dropped," he said.His remarks come amid Pakistan's efforts to attract foreign investment into its mineral sector, particularly in resource-rich regions such as Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.CPEC, a flagship component of China's Belt and Road Initiative, includes infrastructure, energy and industrial development projects. The initiative has faced challenges over the years, including security threats, delays and concerns over the safety of Chinese personnel and investments.
Article Summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman accused Pakistan army of derailing Chinese investments under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor ( CPEC) He alleged that the country's mineral wealth was being used to advance foreign interests and facilitate a shift towards United States.

Article Title: Pakistan's confidence crisis: Government officials plan to move families abroad for secure future
Article Text:
Shehbaz Sharif-led Pakistan govt faces confidence crisis as officials plan to move families abroad.

Pakistan is facing questions over the confidence of its own governing establishment, with defence minister Khawaja Asif alleging that some officials holding important positions in the country are planning to settle abroad, including in Portugal and other Western nations.The reported plans have drawn attention to a wider contradiction for the nation grappled with the economic crisis.While the government expects citizens to remain patient amid the country's difficulties, some people within the administration are said to be looking at opportunities and a more secure future overseas for themselves and their families, reported Greek City Times.The issue goes beyond officials moving abroad after retirement as it also raises questions about whether their families are already preparing to build lives elsewhere through overseas education, residency and eventual settlement.If the children of officials study and settle abroad, their families could become less dependent on Pakistan's institutions, even as those officials continue to hold positions of authority at home.The issue of family members studying abroad is also covered in Pakistan's official disclosure requirements. The Establishment Division's asset declaration form asks government officials to provide details of their children's education, including whether they are studying in Pakistan or overseas.It also seeks information about relevant family assets and expenditure.These requirements do not establish how many officials have sent their children abroad or whether they intend to settle overseas. However, they show that such financial arrangements are considered relevant to official disclosure and scrutiny.The reported plans come against the backdrop of a wider migration trend involving Pakistan's educated and professional workforce.In October, overseas Pakistanis minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain told the National Assembly that more than 1.8 million highly educated and professional people had left Pakistan over the previous three years, Pakistan Today reported.The people who moved abroad included doctors, information technology professionals, engineers, academics and skilled workers from several other sectors. Their departure raises concerns about the country's ability to retain experienced professionals across essential industries.The figures cited by the minister underline the scale of the movement of skilled workers out of Pakistan at a time of unprecendented economic crisis.
Article Summary: Pakistan facing confidence crisis as officials plan to move families abroad. Defence minister Khawaja Asif alleges some officials are planning to settle abroad, including in Portugal and other Western nations. Issue goes beyond officials moving abroad after retirement as it also raises questions about whether their families are already preparing to build lives elsewhere.

Article Title: Pakistan gas crisis: Families return to firewood as LPG prices soar ahead of winter
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan's fuel crisis forces families back to firewood and coal

With natural gas available for barely six hours a day and LPG prices soaring, families in Pakistan’s Rawalpindi are returning to firewood, coal and kerosene to keep their kitchens running as winter approaches.According to a report by The Express Tribune, households are increasingly relying on cheaper alternatives such as discarded furniture wood and sawdust. Residents are also facing steep increases in the cost of LPG cylinders, with a new domestic cylinder selling for PKR13,500 (approx Rs 4644), compared with PKR10,000 (approx Rs 3440) earlier. Refill charges have risen from PKR3,000 (approx Rs 1032) to PKR5,000 (approx Rs 1720), while commercial cylinder refills have nearly doubled to PKR25,000 (approx Rs 8600).The cost of firewood and coal has also climbed. Dry firewood is selling for PKR1,500 (approx Rs 516) to PKR1,800 (approx Rs 619) per maund, while ordinary firewood costs PKR1,300 (approx 447) to PKR1,400 (approx Rs 482). Coal is priced between PKR800 (approx Rs 275) and PKR1,000 (approx Rs 344) per maund, depending on quality, and sawdust costs around PKR700 (approx Rs 240) per maund.Muhammad Faizan, a furniture factory owner, told The Express Tribune that waste wood previously dumped near Nullah Lai was now being collected by residents for cooking.Shehzad Manzoor Kiyani, divisional president of the All-Pakistan Clerks Association, said inflation and unreliable gas supplies had forced government employees to return to firewood and coal. He said households were spending PKR10,000 (approx Rs 3440) to PKR12,000 (approx Rs 4127) a month on LPG.The household crisis comes as Pakistan’s LPG supply faces further pressure. The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) has raised the official LPG price for November to PKR 294,075 (approx Rs 1,01,138) per tonne, from PKR 279,341 (approx Rs 96,084) in October. The price of an 11.8-kg domestic cylinder has consequently risen by PKR 173 (approx Rs 59) to PKR 3,470 (approx Rs 1,194), taking the official retail rate to PKR 294 (approx Rs 101) per kg.But LPG is reportedly selling for as much as PKR 630 (approx Rs 217) per kg in the open market, while company-operated franchises are charging up to PKR 400 (approx Rs 138) per kg. Ogra said the increase followed a 6.47% rise in Saudi Aramco’s contract price, despite a marginal 0.12% decline in the average dollar exchange rate.LPG Distributors Association of Pakistan chairman Irfan Khokhar said the situation was serious because of the closure of the Iran border. He claimed that at least 70% of Pakistan’s LPG was imported from Iran, with the remaining 30% produced locally, and urged the government to curb market manipulation.Meanwhile, the Pakistan LPG Marketers Association has threatened to shut down businesses from November 16 if the government sidelines the private sector under its proposed LPG policy. Association chairman Ali Haider said the government should retain the sector’s deregulated structure, arguing that the private sector played a major role in imports.Haider said that of around 1.3 million tonnes of LPG consumed, approximately 225,000 tonnes were imported from the Gulf, largely by private companies. In a letter to petroleum minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, the association said the draft policy sent to the prime minister had been prepared without private-sector input and called for complete deregulation of the LPG sector.The association also criticised the petroleum development levy of Rs4,669 per tonne on locally produced LPG under the 2016 policy. The levy was intended to help state-owned entities, including Pakistan State Oil, Parco and Sui Southern Gas Company, import LPG during winter and emergencies. Haider alleged that despite billions of rupees being collected through the levy, these entities had failed to import supplies during the current shortage.
Article Summary: Natural gas available for barely six hours a day in Rawalpindi. Families are increasingly relying on cheaper alternatives such as discarded furniture wood and sawdust. Residents are also facing steep increases in the cost of LPG cylinders, with a new domestic cylinder selling for PKR13,500 (approx Rs 4644)

Article Title: India should arm Afghan Taliban against Pakistan: Sushant Sareen
Article Text:
-

India should consider formally recognising the Taliban government in Afghanistan and providing it with military assistance to counter Pakistan, strategic affairs analyst Sushant Sareen has argued, calling for a rethink of New Delhi’s approach to its western neighbourhood.Speaking on Faultline with Ananya Dasgupta on Times Axis, Sareen said India should not allow international consensus to dictate its Afghanistan policy. He argued that if Pakistan was using military force to pressure the Taliban, India should consider helping the Afghan regime defend itself.“If the Afghan Taliban are going to be bullied by the Pakistanis… then maybe we should help them militarily,” Sareen said. “So that they can also hit back.”He went beyond making a general case for military assistance, suggesting that India consider supplying Afghanistan with anti-drone systems, drone technology and missile capabilities.“If you can give them some anti-drone systems to the Afghans, if you can give them maybe some drone technology, which will help them fight back, maybe give them some missile systems or, you know, long-range rocket systems,” Sareen said.“Why not? I think we should consider it so that at least the Pakistanis cannot, you know, bully somebody into submission,” he added, arguing that India needed to be more willing to take risks if it wanted to project power internationally.Sareen’s argument comes against the backdrop of growing tensions between Pakistan and the Taliban, once backed by Islamabad but now increasingly unwilling to follow its instructions. The conflict has exposed the limits of Pakistan’s long-standing effort to exercise strategic influence over Afghanistan.Sareen said India should also reconsider its refusal to formally recognise the Taliban government, which came to power in 2021. He argued that recognition need not mean approval of the regime’s ideology or policies.“Recognition does not mean endorsement,” he said, pointing out that countries maintain diplomatic relations with governments whose actions they do not necessarily agree with.According to Sareen, the Taliban are the de facto rulers of Afghanistan and India already has a degree of engagement with them. He questioned why New Delhi should continue to hold back from formal recognition simply because other countries have not changed their position.Sareen said New Delhi should make its own assessment of what serves Indian interests, rather than remain constrained by concerns about how other countries might react.“The world doesn't ask us for our opinions before they start doing things,” he said.Sareen believes Pakistan’s Afghan strategy has backfired. Islamabad once viewed the Taliban as a means of securing influence in Afghanistan, but the relationship has turned adversarial as the Taliban has asserted its own interests.Explaining the mistake in Pakistan’s calculations, Sareen said Islamabad had mistaken a temporary alliance with sections of the Afghan population for lasting control.“You can rent an Afghan, you can't buy him,” he said, adding that the Afghans acted in Pakistan’s interests only as long as it suited them. Once they gained greater agency, they began pursuing their own priorities.Pakistan accuses the Taliban of providing sanctuary to the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), whose attacks have targeted the Pakistani state. The Taliban, in turn, has resisted pressure from Islamabad and accused Pakistan of backing groups opposed to its rule.Sareen also discussed Pakistan’s interest in the Wakhan Corridor, a narrow strip of Afghan territory that could provide direct connectivity to Central Asia. He said Pakistan appeared to see control of the corridor as a way to gain strategic leverage over the Taliban, but warned that such a move could invite retaliation.For India, Sareen argued, the question is whether the deteriorating relationship between Pakistan and the Taliban creates an opportunity to protect its own strategic interests. He urged New Delhi to consider both diplomatic recognition and military assistance, while acknowledging that a more assertive role would carry risks.His proposal raises a difficult question for Indian policymakers: could a former Pakistani ally now become a strategic counterweight to Islamabad — and is New Delhi prepared to act on that possibility?
Article Summary: India should not allow international consensus to dictate its Afghanistan policy, says Sushant Sareen. He argues that if Pakistan was using military force to pressure the Taliban, India should consider helping the Afghan regime defend itself. He suggests that India consider supplying Afghanistan with anti-drone systems, drone technology and missile capabilities.

Article Title: ‘Koi sharam hoti hai': Pak lawmaker mocks Khawaja Asif after Munir’s Iran visit
Article Text:
Fazl then turned Asif’s own words against him, repeating a phrase the defence minister had previously used to taunt PTI

Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman took a jibe at Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif over Field Marshal Asim Munir’s participation in a high-level regional security meeting in Iran, questioning why the defence minister was absent from the talks.According to a report by Dawn, Fazl raised the issue during his address to the National Assembly on Wednesday, referring to a meeting in Tehran attended by Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, alongside senior officials from Iran, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.“A defence pact is taking shape in Iran, a meeting is under way (there), and the defence minister is sitting here,” Fazl said, drawing laughter and desk-thumping in the House. Pointing to Naqvi’s presence at the meeting, he asked: “The interior minister is required there as well?”Fazl then turned Asif’s own words against him, repeating a phrase the defence minister had previously used to taunt Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).“There is your respect and stature — koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai (have some shame, show some modesty),” he said, breaking into laughter.Responding in the National Assembly on Thursday, Asif denied that a defence pact was being negotiated in Tehran.
